title: Part of #394: Smart Guides display options and Snapping Tolerance
author: wstock
body:
Part of #394. Seven of the Smart Guides preferences that were stored but read by nothing now do what their labels say, for the mouse and for agents (`prefs.set`, then `pointer_gesture`). The issue stays open for the rest.

**Preferences › Smart Guides**
- **Color**: the smart guides' lines and labels take the preference's colour. Its default is now `#ff3dfc`, the magenta the tools have always drawn, so nothing changes until it is edited.
- **Alignment Guides** off: no line is drawn along the edge or centre the art lines up with. The art still snaps into line (these are display options; snapping is unchanged).
- **Anchor/Path Labels** off: no "anchor", "center", "path" or "align" label.
- **Measurement Labels** off: no size or offset readout while drawing (shapes, the freehand family, slices), moving a selection, dragging a ruler guide, or drawing and resizing an artboard.
- **Transform Tools** off: no readout while scaling or rotating with the Selection tool, Free Transform, or the Rotate/Scale/Shear/Reflect tools.
- **Object Highlighting** off: the Selection tools no longer outline the object under the pointer. The outline now also needs View › Smart Guides on, since it is one of their display options.
- **Snapping Tolerance** (0–40 px, 4 by default, as in Illustrator): replaces the 5 px hard-coded for every smart guide snap — drawn points, dragged selections, bounding-box handles, ruler guides, artboards and reference points. Snap to Point keeps its own `snapToPointTolerance`.

**How**
- `vectorcraft_tools::guides::GuideStyle` (colour, lines, labels) rides on `Targets` (`Targets::styled(cx)`), so every snap method draws through two helpers instead of the `MAGENTA` literal; `ToolContext` gains the six fields and `snap_tol()`. The tools gate their `Overlay::Measure` readouts on `measurement_labels` / `transform_tools_guides`.
- The engine fills them from `Prefs` in `with_tool_cx` (the colour parsed with `vectorcraft_color::Color::from_hex`, falling back to magenta);…

title: Part of #451: guides dragged out of the rulers snap, artboard guides
author: bflatastic
body:
Guides dragged out of the rulers now snap like moved guides, and guides can belong to one artboard (parts a–c of #451; part d is still open).

- **Snapping (a, b):** A guide dragged out of a ruler used to snap only with Shift, to the ruler's ticks. The drag now goes through the engine: `Session::ruler_guide` drives a `NewGuide` that previews `guide.add`, and the result is one undo step. With Smart Guides on, it lands on the edges, centres (which covers the sides' midpoints) and anchors of the art, and on the artboards' edges and centres, with a label. With Smart Guides off, View › Snap to Point pulls new and moved guides onto anchors. Shared `GuideSnap` in `rulerguide.rs`, `Targets::anchors_only`.
- **Moving art (b):** with Smart Guides on, art moved with the Selection tool already snapped flush to artboard edges and centres on main. A new test now covers it.
- **Artboard guides (c):** `Guide.artboard` holds an artboard id. The field is written only when set, so canvas guides save as before and older files open unchanged. `guide.add {artboard?: index}` makes one and `guide.list` reports `artboard`. A guide dragged out of a ruler while the Artboard tool is active belongs to the active artboard (Illustrator's rule). An artboard guide is drawn, picked and snapped to (Snap to Point) only across its artboard. It moves with the artboard (`artboard.move`, a pure move in `artboard.setProps`, `artboard.rearrange`), is copied with it (`artboard.duplicate`, Alt-drag copy) and is deleted with it (`artboard.delete`, `artboard.cut`); the guide selection stays in step through `Document::retain_guides`. SVG/PDF export is unchanged, since ruler guides aren't exported.
- **Not done (d):** ruler guides as Layers rows with their own lock and hide. Ruler guides aren't layer nodes, and making them nodes would break their non-printing, not-selectable-as-art semantics. Lock Guides already locks them all (since #415), and Make Guides paths are already `<Guide>` rows in Layers. This is liste…

title: Fix #455: the toolbar's double arrow and Window › Toolbars switch one/two columns
author: bflatastic
body:
The toolbar was forced into two columns whenever the window was shorter than the single column (~990 pt for Basic), so on most screens the double arrow and Window › Toolbars › Single / Double Column changed a flag nothing read.

- The column count is the user's choice alone; a short window scrolls the tools (#84) instead of doubling them.
- `window.toolbarColumns` takes `{double?: bool}` (set or toggle, returns the new state) and reports `checked`; the toolbar's double arrow runs it, so the control channel and MCP do exactly what the click does.
- Window › Toolbars item now reads "Double Column" with a check mark; cs, es, ja, pt-br, zh-hans, zh-hant updated, es `@msg` row for the new error.

title: Fix #457: paste screenshots from the clipboard on macOS, Windows and the web
author: bflatastic
body:
Screenshots and other copied pictures now paste from the system clipboard on macOS, Windows and the web, as embedded images at the view centre.

- **macOS:** Paste (which owns Cmd+V through the native menu) was enabled for text only, so an image-only clipboard pasted nothing; arboard also reads TIFF only. The pasteboard's types (`public.png`, `public.tiff`) now enable Paste, and its PNG, else TIFF, pastes as it is.
- **Windows:** bitmaps came through `CF_BITMAP` + `GetDIBits`, which drops alpha. Paste now reads `PNG`, else `CF_DIBV5`, else `CF_DIB`: a BMP file header is put in front (image's headerless BMP decoder misplaces the pixels after a BITMAPINFOHEADER's masks or colour table), alpha kept, opaque when it is zero throughout (screenshots), capped at 32768 px a side.
- **Web:** only SVG text pasted. A capture-phase `paste` listener hands the first pasted file that is art (`file_flavour`) to the app through the new `VectorcraftApp::paste_from_host`, pasted with the chord held, like the desktop paste keys (not while a field or the Type tool has the keyboard).
- **Linux:** already reads `image/png`; its Paste menu item still waits for text (arboard has no cheap way to ask for a bitmap), the paste keys take one.
- Docs (`mcp.md`, `control-protocol.md`) and ROADMAP updated.

Parity: Illustrator pastes clipboard pictures from other apps as embedded images ([Copy artwork using clipboard](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/edit-objects/copy-artwork-using-clipboard.html), [Move or duplicate objects by pasting](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/arrange-objects/move-or-duplicate-an-object-by-pasting.html)).

title: Type: burasagari — a Japanese comma or full stop ending a line may hang outside it
author: imachus
body:
Japanese hanging punctuation (burasagari): Paragraph panel menu › Burasagari › None / Standard / Forced, and `text.setFormat {burasagari: "none"|"standard"|"forced"}`.

Behaviour, described for a justified frame exactly 20 ems wide (horizontal and vertical alike):

- **None**: a comma or full stop that would be the 21st character can't start a line, so it goes to the next line with the character before it (the line keeps 19 characters, spread).
- **Standard**: a comma or full stop that doesn't fit hangs outside the frame (the line takes 21 characters). One that fits (the 20th) stays inside.
- **Forced**: a comma or full stop ending a line always hangs, also when it would fit; the characters before it fill the measure.
- Only 、 and 。 hang. Closing brackets (」 etc.) don't, even with Forced.
- The hanging mark takes the width its mojikumi gives it (half width at a line end with Line-end Punctuation Half Width).

Implementation:

- `ParaStyle::burasagari` (`Burasagari::{None, Standard, Forced}`), saved only when not None, so older files and builds are unaffected. New type takes **Standard**; documents from before it and imported text keep None.
- `break_line`: with Standard or Forced, a 、 or 。 that overflows ends the line when kinsoku allows a break after it.
- `flow`: on area type, a 、 or 。 ending the line hangs (Standard: when the line is longer than the measure; Forced: always). The line is aligned and justified without it, and it follows the last character. Point type, RTL and hyphenated lines are left alone.
- A paragraph with burasagari on *and* a 、 or 。 in it is composed line by line (the every-line composer works on word spaces). Latin paragraphs keep the every-line composer with the new default (`tests_typo::burasagari_keeps_the_every_line_composer_for_latin_text`).
- Labels: ja, zh-hans, zh-hant, es (catalogs that must be complete).

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger, so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` it reaches is discarded, including the panic reports `guard.rs` turns into `log::error!` and the renderer choice. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them. (`crates/mcp/src/logging.rs` only installs a logger in `vectorcraft-cli`; the desktop app does not link it, so the two never share a process.)

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere.

## What

`apps/vectorcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/vectorcraft.log` next to `ui.json` (Linux `~/.config/vectorcraft/logs/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/VectorCraft/logs/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\VectorCraft\logs\`).
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `vectorcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512, with a "N earlier lines dropped" note); when no file can be attached the buffer is released.
- **Levels:** `info` for `vectorcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.
- **`VECTORCRAFT_NO_PREFS`:** runs with it log to standard error only, so agent and test runs don't rotate away the user's logs (the same rule Data Recovery follows).

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first; the file is attached after argument parsing (new `log_dir()`), so `--version` leaves no …

title: AI import: groups and nested groups survive
author: bflatastic
body:
Addresses Discord feedback: old `.ai` files lost their group structure when opened.

- **Legacy PostScript `.ai` (Illustrator 3–8, and their EPS):** read by the EPS interpreter, which only recorded what was drawn. In a file in Illustrator's format (`%AI…` comments, or Illustrator as the creator) the `u` … `U` written at the top level now open and close groups, whatever the prolog defines them as. Groups come in nested as they were, between and inside clipping groups; a fill and stroke of one path in a group stay one object; `U` without a `u` does nothing.
- **`clipnest`:** `Clip` now holds an optional region. Without one it's a plain group, nested in the same chain as the clips (ids are handed out in opening order, so a mixed chain sorts by id).
- **Hardening (existing crash):** clips nested without limit used to nest clipping groups until the stack overflowed, in both EPS and EMF/WMF import. Clips and groups now nest at most 128 deep, with a warning, and each object's chain counts against the EPS drawing budget.
- **PDF-compatible `.ai` (Illustrator 9+), not possible:** the PDF content draws each object in its own `q … cm … Q` and only marks layers (`/OC`), clipping groups and groups with opacity, blending or a mask. Those already come back. Plain groups exist only in the private data, which is out of scope. ROADMAP's out-of-scope note and `docs/mcp.md` now say so.
- Tests: `eps/src/import/tests_illustrator.rs` (nested groups, an Illustrator 3 header, a prolog whose groups gsave/grestore, groups mixed with clips, fill+stroke merge, a non-Illustrator `u`, unbalanced and over-deep groups), deep-clip tests for EPS and EMF, an engine `document.open` test, and the hostile-PostScript fuzz extended with Illustrator headers and `u`/`U` tokens. ROADMAP and `docs/mcp.md` are updated.

title: Control bar: image controls (Image Trace, Embed, Crop, Mask) when an image is selected
author: bflatastic
body:
Addresses Discord feedback: Image Trace and the other image options were hidden when an image was selected. Copy an image, paste it, then Image Trace now works from the Control bar, as in Illustrator.

- **Control bar, one image selected:** Linked File or Embedded, then the file name, colour mode and PPI, then Embed (and Edit Original) or Unembed…, an **Image Trace** split button (a click traces with the Default preset; the arrow lists the 12 presets and traces with the one you pick), **Mask** and **Crop Image**. These replace Fill and Stroke for images. Opacity, Style, Align and X/Y/W/H stay.
- **Control bar, one Image Trace object selected:** "Image Tracing", its **Preset** dropdown (picking another preset traces it again), a button that opens the Image Trace panel, and **Expand**.
- **Properties panel:** Quick Actions has Image Trace (split button), Crop Image and Mask for an image. An Image Trace object gets an Image Trace section with Preset, Expand and Release. The Embed and Unembed buttons are shared with the Control bar (`place::link_buttons`).
- **New engine command `object.maskImage` ("Mask", no menu path, reachable over MCP and the control channel):** clips the selected image with a clipping path along its outline (rotated with the image) and selects that path, so dragging its handles crops the image. One undo step.
- **New widget:** `widgets::split_button`, a flat button with a menu arrow.
- **Translations:** new strings added to es, ja, zh-hans and zh-hant. "Mask" also added to pt-br and cs.
- **Not done:** Image Trace's View modes (Outlines, Source Image), because the engine can't render them yet; they are listed in the ROADMAP parity row. Crop Image still crops to the artboard, as the menu item does; there is no on-canvas crop box yet.

Parity sources: [Image tracing presets](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/image-trace-presets.html), [Image Trace panel options](https://helpx.adobe.com/lv/illustrator/using/tracing-artwork-live-trace-or.html),…

title: Pen and anchors: Alt edits one handle, cut and convert selected anchors from the Control bar
author: bflatastic
body:
Addresses Discord feedback: Alt with the Pen didn't change one Bézier handle on its own, and a CorelDRAW user couldn't break a curve at a point to pull it apart.

- **Pen + Alt** over a handle end or an anchor of a selected path (the one being drawn too) works as the Anchor Point tool, with the convert cursor. Dragging a handle moves only that handle, clicking a smooth anchor makes it a corner, and dragging an anchor pulls out new symmetric handles. Drawing then goes on. Alt held on empty canvas still draws as before. Handles hidden by a partial anchor selection can't be grabbed (this also applies to the Anchor Point tool).
- **`path.cutAtAnchors`** (Cut Path at Selected Anchor Points) is one undo step and answers `{ids}`. A closed path opens at the cut. An open path becomes one path per piece. One of each cut's two coincident anchors stays selected, so a Direct Selection drag or `path.moveAnchors` pulls the ends apart. When only open ends are selected it refuses and leaves no undo step.
- **`path.convertAnchors {to}`** validates `to` and skips stale anchor refs (it used to index past them). Converting an anchor that is already smooth keeps its handles.
- **DRY:** new `SubPath::cut_at` and `SubPath::smooth_anchor` in geom now back `path.split` (Scissors), `path.cutAtAnchors`, `path.convertAnchor` and `path.convertAnchors`. They replace three copies of the same logic.
- **UI:** when anchors are selected, the Control bar and the Properties panel show "Convert:" (corner, smooth) and "Anchors:" (remove, connect = Join, cut). The two groups sit inline in the Control bar and one per row in the panel, and both share one widget function. Cut Path is also on the contextual task bar (where it replaces Offset Path and Simplify) and in the canvas context menu. There is one new original icon, `dc-anchor-smooth.svg`, with its ASSETS.md row.
- **i18n:** ja, zh-hans, zh-hant and es strings, plus cs for the context-menu item and es `@msg` rows. Also a new docs/mcp.md section and ROA…

title: Part of #394: Type Object Selection by Path Only
author: wstock
body:
Part of #394. Follows #453; the next stored-but-unused option, as one small PR.

**Type › Type Object Selection by Path Only** (off by default) now acts. On, the Selection tools pick type on its *type path* only, within Selection & Anchor Display › Tolerance:

- point type: its baseline — the line the selection marks under it, across the width of its layout;
- area type: its frame;
- type on a path: its path.

A click among the glyphs or inside the frame or path selects nothing. Off, anywhere in the type's bounds selects it, as before. The option reaches everything that hit-tests type through the same options — the Selection tools (and `pointer_gesture` for agents), Command Click to Select Objects Behind, object highlighting and the canvas context menu.

Parity source (feature name only): helpx "Select objects" › Type Object Selection by Path Only — select type by clicking the type path rather than anywhere on the characters.

- `ToolContext.type_path_only` → `hit_options()`; filled from `prefs.type_selection_by_path_only` in `tooling.rs`; the canvas's `hit_at` reads the same preference.
- ROADMAP ("Shipped so far", the prefs count 38 → 37, the UI chrome row) and `docs/mcp.md` (Type preferences: `typeSelectionByPathOnly`).

**Tests**

title: Part of #472: Escape leaves Presentation Mode; dropped documents open as tabs; .ai off-artboard note
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes the release-blocking Presentation Mode trap and the drop behaviour from #472, and explains the missing off-artboard art in Illustrator files (partial: that art is only in Illustrator's private data).

- **Presentation Mode (blocker):** Escape leaves it (as in Illustrator, [helpx: viewing artwork](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/viewing-artwork.html) "To exit this mode, press Esc"); F from it goes back to Normal Screen Mode. The screen mode is no longer saved with the preferences (`#[serde(skip)]`), so the app always starts in Normal Screen Mode and old preferences saved in Presentation Mode open normally. `ui.inspect` reports `screenMode` on its own.
- **Drag and drop:** desktop drags carry no pointer position or modifiers (winit 0.30's Windows `IDropTarget`, macOS `NSDraggingDestination` and X11 XDND emit only `HoveredFile`/`DroppedFile`), so the stale/absent position was taken for the middle of the canvas and every drop was placed. Now, where the platform doesn't give a position, a document (native, SVG, PDF, `.ai`, EPS, DXF, EMF/WMF) opens as a tab of its own and a picture or text is placed in the middle of the view; pictures dropped with documents are placed first so the last document opened is shown. The web (whose drag events carry the position) keeps Illustrator's target choice: placed on the canvas (linked, Shift embeds), opened when dropped off it on the tab bar ([community: drag to the tab bar to open](https://community.adobe.com/t5/illustrator-discussions/illustrator-opens-up-in-new-tab-when-dragging-images/td-p/13394861)). `drop_files` now takes a target per file; the canvas highlight follows the same rule.
- **Art outside the artboard (.ai/.pdf):** Illustrator's PDF-compatible part leaves out art outside the artboards; it lives only in the AIPrivateData streams ([community](https://community.adobe.com/t5/illustrator-discussions/where-is-pdf-info-outiside-of-artboards/m-p/9698454)), which are undocumented and out of scope (ROADMAP › Out o…

title: Part of #394: Anti-aliased Artwork
author: wstock
body:
Part of #394. One small PR for one stored-but-unused option, after #453 and #475.

**General › Anti-aliased Artwork** (on by default) now acts on the canvas. Off, the art is drawn with hard edges — a pixel is painted when a path, text or image covers at least half of it — while raster effects (blur, shadows, glows) and pattern tiles stay smooth, which is what `vectorcraft_render::AntiAlias::None` already did for exports. On, `AntiAlias::Art`, as before. Exports keep their own Anti-aliasing option (Export, Save for Web, Rasterize).

Parity source (feature name only): helpx "General preferences" › Anti-aliased Artwork, which smooths the on-screen edges of vector art.

**Changes**
- `canvas.rs`: the frame's `RenderOptions.anti_alias` follows `prefs.anti_aliased_artwork`.
- `CacheKey` gains `anti_alias`, so toggling the preference re-renders the art rather than reusing the cached raster.
- ROADMAP ("Shipped so far", the prefs count 38 → 37, the UI chrome row) and `docs/mcp.md` (the view preferences: `antiAliasedArtwork`).

**Tests**
- `canvas::tests::anti_aliased_artwork_preference_smooths_the_canvas`: a headless frame renders a disc; the test reads the art's raster back out of the frame's `TexturesDelta`. On: edge pixels with partial alpha; a frame with nothing changed uploads nothing; off: every pixel fully painted or not (and the disc still painted); on again: smooth. The `shapes()` helper now shares a `frame_output()` that returns the textures too.
- `cargo test -p vectorcraft-ui-egui`: 702 passed. Clippy on ui-egui is clean apart from the pre-existing `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` in `cursors.rs` (#444, rust 1.99), untouched here.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Part of #394: Show Pixel Grid (Above 600% Zoom)
author: wstock
body:
Part of #394. One small PR for one stored-but-unused option, after #453, #475 and #477.

**Guides & Grid › Show Pixel Grid (Above 600% Zoom)** (on by default) now acts. In View › Pixel Preview at 600% zoom and above, the canvas draws a translucent grey line at every document pixel, over the art, so the pixels the art rasterizes to can be seen. Nothing is drawn below 600%, out of Pixel Preview, or with the option off.

**Changes**
- `canvas.rs`: after the document grid that sits over the art, the pixel grid at a 1 pt spacing through the same `grid()` (so it thins and clips the same way), gated on `view.pixel_preview && zoom >= 6.0 && prefs.show_pixel_grid`. Colour is a fixed translucent grey (`PIXEL_GRID`), the threshold `PIXEL_GRID_ZOOM`.

title: EPS import: other apps' EPS open as vectors, a preview that stands in says why
author: bflatastic
body:
Addresses Discord feedback ("EPS files are always rasterized: they open as bitmaps, in other programs as vectors"). Refs #466. Refs #469 (its creator is still unknown: an Illustrator file is likely fixed here, a CorelDRAW or Affinity file is only covered by synthetic programs). Fixes #474.

On main, every EPS saved by Illustrator 2026 fell back to its TIFF preview (`gcheck` unknown), its Illustrator 8 format failed with "typecheck in `a dictionary`" (#474), Inkscape/cairo files stopped at their first image (`status`), and the warning didn't say where the program failed.

title: Part of #394: Numbers Without Units Are Points
author: wstock
body:
Part of #394. Preferences › Units › **Numbers Without Units Are Points** (`numbersWithoutUnitsArePoints`) was stored and never read (#67 noted it as "no effect yet").

**Now**
- On: a number typed with no unit into any length field (`num_field`, `opt_field`, and the spin fields built on them — Transform, Properties, Control bar, Stroke, dialogs) is read in points whatever the field's unit. A typed unit still wins (`12 mm`, `1in`, `2p6`), arithmetic too (`10+5` → 15 pt), and the field keeps showing its value in its own unit with the suffix.
- Off (the default): a bare number is in the field's unit, as before.
- The app sets the frame's rule from the preference in `VectorcraftApp::logic` and the fields read it through the egui context (`widgets::typed_unit`), so none of the 45 field call sites change.

**Default flipped from `true` to `false`.** Illustrator's option is off by default, and `false` is the behaviour the fields had while the option was unread — keeping `true` would have turned every bare number in a millimetre field into points for everyone on the next build. Users whose saved preferences carry the old stored `true` will see bare numbers read as points until they untick the option; happy to add a one-off migration if you'd rather not have that.

**Tests**
- `tests_numfields::bare_numbers_are_points_when_the_preference_says_so` (headless egui field in millimetres): off → `12` is 12 mm; on → `12` is 12 pt, `12 mm` / `1in` / `10+5` as expected; off again → millimetres.

title: Fix #483: Shift-drag marquees toggle the selection; the Lasso's Alt keeps the rest
author: bflatastic
body:
A Shift-drag marquee only ever added to the selection; as in Illustrator it now toggles what it reaches, so selected objects (or anchors) can be taken out with a marquee.

- **Selection tool**: the Shift marquee runs `select.toggle`, which now takes `{ids}` too (each one toggles); a Shift-click on empty canvas still leaves the selection alone.
- **Direct Selection / Group Selection**: the Shift marquee toggles the anchors inside it (`select.anchorsMany` mode `toggle`); a path left with none leaves the selection, one with all of them is selected whole again.
- **`select.anchorsMany`** takes `mode: "set"|"add"|"toggle"|"subtract"` (`add: true` still means add; an unknown mode is a parameter error). Adding anchors of a path selected whole keeps it whole, and references outside the path are ignored.
- **Lasso**: Shift adds and Alt subtracts through the same command, so an Alt lasso no longer drops selected type, groups and other non-path objects from the selection.
- Docs (`docs/mcp.md`, with a `pointer_gesture` example), ROADMAP (Last updated, Selection bullet), command-sweep cases for the new modes.

Illustrator reference: Shift-click or Shift-drag around objects adds or removes them from the selection ([Select objects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/select-objects/select-transform-objects-selection-tools.html)); the Lasso adds with Shift and subtracts with Alt/Option ([Select anchor points](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/select-anchor-points-in-paths.html)).

## Checks

title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![VectorCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/vectorcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the VectorCraft colour field, VectorCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small VectorCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg` is the only image source (~35 KB). Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `package.sh` renders it at packaging time with [resvg](https://github.com/linebender/resvg) (1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800), joins both into a HiDPI TIFF with `tiffutil -cathidpicheck`, and copies it plus `DS_Store` (Finder view settings: window 660×400 content, icon size 128, app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background) into the staging folder. The image is still built with `hdiutil makehybrid`: no committed bitmap, no mounted device, no Finder scripting on CI.
- `release.yml` installs resvg 0.48.1 on the macOS runner (`cargo install resvg --version 0.48.1 --locked`).
- `packaging/macos/dmg/README.md` explains the layout, the rules and how to change the design.

## One behaviour change: the volume name drops the version

`.DS_Store` points at the background through an alias that includes the volume name. With `VectorCraft <version>` Finder kept the window and icon positions but lost the background (tested). So the mounted volume is now called `VectorCraft`; the DMG file name still carries the version.

## Tested

- Built the image with the exact `package.sh` steps (resvg render + `tiffutil`, staging folder, `makehybrid`, UDZO) around a stub `VectorCraft.app` with the real icon, mounted it and opened it in Finder on macOS: the screenshot above is t…

title: Part of #491: pen taps click where they tap; Linux note for tablet pens on Wayland
author: bflatastic
body:
Tablet pens on KDE Plasma 6.3+ under Wayland can't reach the app until eframe moves to winit 0.31; this documents the workarounds and fixes a pen/touch tap bug on our side.

- **Root cause (upstream):** winit 0.30 binds no Wayland tablet protocol (`zwp_tablet_v2`), and since Plasma 6.3 KWin no longer emulates pointer input for such clients ([kwin!6336](https://invent.kde.org/plasma/kwin/-/merge_requests/6336); KWin's `input.cpp` returns early unless `KWIN_WAYLAND_EMULATE_TABLET=1`). The pen moves KWin's cursor, the window gets no events, matching the report. Tablet input is in winit 0.31 ([winit#4318](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4318)); egui's move is [egui#7731](https://github.com/emilk/egui/pull/7731) (draft).
- **Docs:** `docs/development.md` › Linux: Wayland and X11 and the README give the workarounds: run under XWayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY= vectorcraft`, or the launcher's `Exec=`), or set `KWIN_WAYLAND_EMULATE_TABLET=1` for the session. Pressure: Windows only (winit 0.30).
- **Canvas (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`):** egui-winit turns a pen/finger touch into a mouse and sends `PointerGone` when it lifts. A tap pressed and lifted in one frame had no hover position, so the canvas ignored it, and a release without a pointer position ended the drag at the canvas's centre. Press and double-tap now fall back to the interact position, and release to the last position seen during the drag.
- **Tests:** headless frames replay a pen's event sequence (Touch + emulated pointer): a Pencil stroke lands where the pen went and Bloat with Use Pressure Pen journals each sample's pressure; a one-frame tap selects without moving anything (fails without the fix).
- **ROADMAP:** Last updated, the Platforms row, the hardening gap, the input/pressure note.

`Part of #491`: the Wayland pen itself needs winit 0.31, so the issue stays open.

body:

body:

Plain box selection and Shift-clicking empty canvas keep their existing behavior. `select.toggle` accepts an `ids` batch while retaining the existing `id` form; repeated IDs toggle once. title: Fix #498, #505: Illustrator EPS images aren't banded, text effects open as vectors
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #498: colour images in EPS saved by Illustrator CS and later came in as sheared horizontal bands. Fixes #505: Illustrator EPS text effects fell back to their preview. #505's report has no file or error message, so this is likely but not confirmed. Two commits, one per issue. They're in one PR because #505's effect rasters need #498's fix too.

**#498** (`a303add7`)
- **Cause:** Illustrator writes a colour image with one data source per ink: four procedures that each read one row of their ink from the same file, called by `image` in turn (C, M, Y, K, C …). The reader drained each source on its own, so the cyan plane took the first rows of all four inks.
- **Fix:** image data sources are read in turn (a procedure once a round, a file or string a row a round) by one reader, `read_sources`. Single sources, procedure filters and masked images now use it too.
- **Tests** (`tests_images.rs`):
  - procedures reading one file, in the dictionary and `colorimage` operand forms (fails on main);
  - separate string sources;
  - rows padded to a byte at 1/2/4/12/16 bits with an odd width;
  - PNG predictors with every row filter.

**#505** (`262caec2`)
- **Cause 1:** Illustrator's procsets count each `save` in a dictionary and raise `limitcheck` at 64, relying on `restore` to put the count back. `restore` didn't undo dictionary changes, so any file with more than 64 images (the rasters of drop shadows and glows on type) fell back to its preview.
  - **Fix:** `restore` now undoes dictionary changes made since the `save` (`def`, `store`, `put`, `undef`, dictionary `copy`), newest first. They're kept in a journal while a save is open, counted against the memory budget. Restoring a save twice raises `invalidrestore`.
- **Cause 2:** in the Illustrator 8 format, pattern fills divide by the largest glyph `cachestatus` reports, which was 0. It now returns realistic font-cache sizes.
- **Cause 3:** type in reencoded font copies (`/Impact*1`) was set in the fallback font. The `*N` su…

title: Fix: check the system clipboard off the UI thread
author: omellado-gh
body:
## What and why

The app checks the system clipboard every 0.25 s to decide whether the Paste menu
items are enabled. On X11, `arboard`'s clipboard read waits up to 4 s for a
`SelectionNotify`; when the clipboard owner never answers (a hung or foreign app,
a clipboard manager, XWayland), that call ran on the UI thread and froze the whole
frame loop — the window stopped drawing and could not be closed.

Reproduced with the real failure: seed the clipboard and stop its owner
(`printf x | xclip -selection clipboard; kill -STOP $(pgrep -x xclip)`), then open
a document. The app became unresponsive and a control-channel `ui.inspect` timed out
while the main thread sat in arboard's wait loop.

This change moves the check off the UI thread: a `clipboard_probe` worker owns a
second clipboard handle, publishes whether Paste has something to take
(`has(PASTE_ORDER)`) over a channel, and wakes the UI only when the verdict changes.
`logic_frame` reads the latest verdict with `try_recv` and never blocks. Without a
factory (the web, and hosts that don't install one) the check stays in line,
throttled, exactly as before. The factory is installed on Linux only for now;
macOS and Windows keep the in-line check, so their behaviour is unchanged.

## How it was tested

- New tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_sysclip_probe.rs` (5): a fake clipboard
  whose `has()` blocks proves the headless UI frame does not wait on it (measured
  elapsed time) and that the check runs on the `vectorcraft-clip` probe thread; the
  probe's verdict enables the Paste menu; a probe that reports nothing leaves it
  disabled; dropping the app stops the probe; and the in-line path (no factory) still
  works. `cargo test -p vectorcraft-ui-egui --lib` → 717 passed.
- End to end with the real X11 hang: with the clipboard owner stopped with `SIGSTOP`
  and a document open, the app stays responsive (`ui.inspect` answers in ~0 ms, main
  thread in its normal `epoll` wait), where before it froze.
- `cargo check -p ve…

title: Fix #494: Pen + Cmd edits the path being drawn; Pen + Alt reshapes segments; handle drags fixed and fast
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #494: path editing in place while drawing with the Pen, Ctrl on Windows and Cmd on the Mac, the way Illustrator does it. Also segment reshaping with Pen + Alt, and the handle drags that sometimes missed or felt slow.

- **Pen + Cmd/Ctrl** ([Illustrator: Ctrl/Cmd lends the last-used selection tool while drawing](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-curves-with-the-pen-tool.html)): the borrowing has moved from the canvas into the engine (`Session::pointer`), so MCP `pointer_gesture` with `mods.cmd` reaches it too. You get the selection tool chosen last, or Direct Selection for the Pen, Curvature and anchor tools until one has been chosen. The Pen isn't deactivated during the borrow, so once you release it goes on drawing the same path, as long as that path stays selected. It won't draw on another open path that gets selected in the meantime. While Cmd is held the pointer is the borrowed tool's.
- **Pen + Alt over a segment** reshapes it, the way the Anchor Point tool does ([Anchor Point tool: reshape segment, Pen + Alt](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tool-techniques/anchor-point-tool.html)).
- **The handles you see are the ones you can drag.** Direct Selection, the Anchor Point tool and Pen + Alt now share one helper.
  - Direct Selection can drag the handles of a path selected as a whole. That's how the Pen leaves a path, so Cmd-drag on a handle while drawing used to miss and deselect.
  - The Anchor Point tool no longer grabs handles hidden by *Show handles when multiple anchors are selected*.
  - The nearest handle wins.
  - A handle shorter than the tolerance leaves its anchor pickable.
  - The anchor tools pick within *Selection & Anchor Display › Tolerance* instead of a fixed 4 px.
- **`path.reshapeSegment`** keeps a smooth anchor at either end smooth (its other handle turns with the moved one) instead of kinking it ([Direct Selection: drag a segment](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tool-te…

title: Fix #502: no startup crash on dual-GPU Linux desktops under Wayland
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #502: on a Linux desktop whose KDE Wayland compositor runs on the NVIDIA GPU, 0.5.0 rendered on the Ryzen's integrated GPU (the low-power default from #329) and crashed at startup.

**Root cause**
- `apps/vectorcraft/src/main.rs` (0.5.0) set `power_preference = LowPower` on every platform. egui-wgpu passed the window surface to `request_adapter`, and wgpu-core kept only the adapters whose surface capabilities query succeeded (`wgpu-core-30.0.1/src/instance.rs:527-546`). RADV passes that check, so the integrated GPU was sorted first (`instance.rs:571-574`), ahead of the order Mesa's device-select layer gives.
- The first swapchain hands KWin buffers allocated on the AMD GPU. KWin can't import them ("importing the supplied dmabufs failed"), which is a fatal Wayland protocol error for the whole connection. The next surface configuration gets `ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR`, `get_default_config` returns `None`, and `egui-wgpu-0.36.2/src/winit.rs:129` panics on `.expect("The surface isn't supported by this adapter")`.

**Change**
- **Preferences › Performance › Graphics Processor** gains **Automatic**, which is now the default. On Windows and macOS it is power saving, as #306 needed. On Linux it keeps the system's order, where Mesa's device-select layer puts the GPU the desktop runs on first. The values are now `automatic`, `lowPower` and `highPerformance` (WebGPU's names). 0.5.0 saved `powerSaving` for everyone, so that value reads as `automatic` (`prefs_dialog::restore`, and the app at startup).
- `apps/vectorcraft/src/gpu.rs` picks the window's adapter through eframe's `native_adapter_selector`, using a pure `adapter_order`:
  - adapters that can't present to the surface are never tried;
  - the adapter named by `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` comes first;
  - hardware before software, native backends before OpenGL, then the power preference, keeping the system's order among equals.
  - Every adapter and the one picked are logged.
- `eframe::run_native` now runs under the engine g…

title: Clean-room: never run, automate or observe Adobe software
author: bflatastic
body:
Adobe's General Terms of Use (Section 17) forbid reverse engineering, including observing a program's inputs and outputs in order to recreate it. The agent rules (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md) allowed "black-box observation of the running app with synthetic documents". This replaces that with an absolute rule from the project owner:

- Never launch, run, script, automate, screenshot or measure Illustrator or any other Adobe application, never compare against one, never make test files with one.
- Never read inside an Adobe install; never copy Adobe-authored code or text (PostScript procsets/prologs, sample files) into the repo, tests included — test inputs are written from the public specifications.
- Behaviour comes only from public documentation and published specs (cited by URL) and from files users send us that they own (local only, never committed).

Follow-ups already in progress: replacing EPS tests that reproduced Adobe procset code with spec-written ones, an own UI palette in place of measured values, a README/NOTICE trademark disclaimer, and a `cargo xtask cleanroom` CI check.

## Checks

title: Fix #501: a Pen drag out of the first anchor always closes the path
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #501. Closing a path with the Pen by dragging out of its first anchor flickered, and if you released while the closing curve was hidden, the shape stayed open. **Stacked on #517** (`fix/issue-494`, which touches the same Pen code), so this PR's base is that branch. GitHub retargets it to `main` once #517 merges.

- **Cause:** the press decided on a close, but every drag move asked again which path was being drawn. The closing preview leaves the path closed, so the Pen no longer counted it as the path it extends. The move then fell through to "first anchor of a new path", and the next move went back to closing. The release committed whichever preview came last.
- **Fix:** the press records what it placed (`Place`: the anchor, the path it goes on, or none for a new path, and whether it closes that path). The drag only shapes that anchor's handles, and the release closes the path wherever the pointer ends up. Handles are symmetric by default and Alt breaks them. This matches Illustrator: [dragging from the start point shapes the closing curve](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-curves-with-the-pen-tool.html).
- **Tests:**
  - tools: the drag sees the path already closed and keeps previewing the close.
  - engine: the path stays closed through all 12 moves of the drag, there is still one path, and the handles at the release are symmetric.
  - mcp: a headless `pointer_gesture` drag closes the path.

title: Type (#432): new type in a Japanese interface starts top-to-top with em box centre alignment
author: imachus
body:
Implements option 2 from #432: while the interface is in Japanese, *new* type starts with em box top-to-top leading (`LeadingModel::EmBoxTop`) and em box centre character alignment (`CharAlign::EmBoxCenter`). In other languages new type keeps the Roman baseline, so Latin area type doesn't move. Closes #432.

**How the engine knows the language.** The UI resolves `interfaceLanguage` (including `auto` → the system's) and now hands the result to the engine each frame as `Session::ui_language`. Without a UI (CLI, headless MCP) an explicit `interfaceLanguage` preference counts; `auto` there means the Roman defaults. `Session::japanese_interface()` reads it.

**Where it applies** (the points listed in #432):
- `text.create` and `text.createInPath`, which the Type tools' clicks and drags (point, area and path type) go through. Both also take `leadingModel` and `charAlign` to choose explicitly. The values used are noted in the journal (`Session::note_journal`), so replaying an action gives the same type in any language.
- `paraStyle.new` / `charStyle.new` when the style is made from nothing (no `attrs`, no text selected): a paragraph style gets `leading_model: emBoxTop`, a character style `charAlign: emBoxCenter`. A style made from selected text still copies that text.
- Imported text (PDF, SVG, DXF…) is untouched and keeps the Roman baseline; saved documents keep exactly what they say (both values are only written when set).

**Docs:** a "New type in a Japanese interface" section in `docs/mcp.md` (with the new `text.create` params), the `text.create` / `text.createInPath` param docs, and a note in the ROADMAP.

title: Fix #506: drawing tools snap to Smart Guides as the Selection tool does
author: bflatastic
body:
The drawing tools now snap to Smart Guides as the Selection tool does, all through one snapper (`guides::DrawSnap`).

- **Pen, Curvature, Pencil:** each anchor (the Pencil's first and last point) lands on other objects' anchors, centres and paths ("anchor", "center", "path") or lines up with their anchors, edges and centres ("align"). The Pen also lands on the path being drawn, and its rubber band ends where the click will go. Hovering shows the guides before the press.
- **Shape tools** (Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Star, Line Segment, Arc, Spiral, the grids): the start point and the dragged corner or radius snap, with guides on hover, at the press and while dragging. The W/H label now gives the size drawn (Alt from the centre, Shift square). Fixes the dragged corner sticking to the shape's own preview: targets were gathered on every drag step from the previewed document.
- **Shift** keeps a point to its 45° step from Constrain Angle (a box: its diagonal) and slides it along that line into alignment with the nearest target.
- **Preferences › Smart Guides › Construction Guides and Angles** now do something: a drawn point near a guide line through the point it leaves from lands on that line, or where a target's alignment line crosses it.
- **Type tool** click and frame, and the **Artboard** tool's new artboard, snap the same way.
- **Direction handles:** #494's `HandleSnap` now wraps a `DrawSnap` holding `Targets::for_handle` for the drag, so there is one cache and one nearest-point lookup.
- **Performance:** targets are gathered once per document state, keyed on the document's uid and revision (new `ToolContext::revision`), from the art in the window. They are sorted, so each pointer move finds nearby targets by bisection instead of a scan. Excluding objects no longer costs an `ancestry` lookup per node (quadratic): one pruned walk does it, which also speeds up the Selection tool's moves and resizes.

title: Fix #508: PDF/.ai import keeps type strokes, wrapped lines and layer order
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes the import problems in #508 (layer order, a stray page layer, outline strokes split from their type, wrapped lines, barcode digits).

- **Stray "Page 2" layer:** a line of type still being gathered when a layer's marked content ended was emitted after the group was popped, so it landed on the page layer. It is now finished before the sequence ends. A clip that opens in one layer and closes in the next (`… EMC /OC /MC1 BDC EMC Q`) now stays in the layer its art was drawn in, so a later empty layer no longer takes it.
- **Layer order:** top-level layers were stacked by first painted art, so a layer that is empty on page 1 and painted only on page 2 ended up on top. Layers now stack in the order the pages mark them (BDC order, merged across pages), and layers that are marked but have no art come in empty.
- **Outline strokes / "LEAD CLIP" not editable:** the file writes a stroke added to a type object as each glyph's outline, stroked one path at a time, right after the text. The importer records each glyph's ink box. Stroked paths that match them one for one become the type object's appearance stroke, above the characters, or below them when drawn first. The type is one editable object again.
- **Barcode text:** digit groups are positioned with `Td` jumps of about 0.6 and 0.36 em. One even tracking value spread those gaps over every digit. A space read from a gap now gets its own tracking when even tracking would move the glyphs after it by more than 0.1 em. Lines are also measured to their last visible glyph, so a trailing space no longer leaks into the tracking.
- **Long text as separate lines:** consecutive lines that share a left edge, font, size, angle and look, step down by one leading, and have at least one line ending in a space are rebuilt as one area type object, left aligned or justified, with paragraph spacing taken from the larger steps. This happens only when laying the text out in that frame reproduces every line break and baseline. If not (for exa…

title: Control bar: Transform link opens the Transform panel;
author: dbambus
body:
## What

title: Fix #511: Live Corners on any path's corners (stars, polygons, pen paths)
author: bflatastic
body:
Live Corners showed only on live rectangles. Now a star, a live polygon and a pen path show corner widgets and round their corners with the same command and geometry.

- **Root cause:** `CornerWidgets::of` returned nothing unless the selected path's live shape was a `LiveShape::Rectangle`, and `object.setLiveShape` only edited rectangle radii. A star is a plain path, so neither selection tool ever showed widgets on it.
- **Geometry (`geom::corners`):** finds a path's corners: anchors with no handles where two straight sides meet (not an open path's ends, not smooth anchors, not anchors where the sides run straight on). It cuts them round, inverted round or chamfered. Every round corner is a circle tangent to both sides, and each corner has its own limit: the cut can reach at most halfway along its shorter side. Rectangles now use this code too. Before the old version was removed, a test compared both versions across sizes, radii and kinds, and the anchors and layout came out bit-identical.
- **Model (`doc::corners`):** `LiveCorners` and `set_corners` handle rectangle, polygon and plain-path corners the same way:
  - Live polygons get `radii`/`kinds`. A radius shared by all corners carries over when the side count changes.
  - Other paths get a new `LiveShape::Path` that keeps the uncut outline, so the corners stay editable. Once no corner is cut, the path goes back to a plain path.
  - Radii scale with transforms (Scale Corners) and corners stay circular.
- **Command:** `object.setLiveShape` takes `corners` as anchor indices of the uncut path. Rectangles keep 0–3. Index ranges are checked and a bad index returns an error.
- **Tools and UI:**
  - Direct Selection shows widgets on any path: every corner, or only the corners holding selected anchors. The Selection tool shows them on live rectangles and polygons.
  - The widgets sit on each corner's bisector, the drag follows it, and corners at their limit are outlined in red.
  - The angle preference, View › Hide Corne…

title: Fix #498, part of #505: EPS image sources read in turn, restore undoes dictionary changes (PLRM)
author: bflatastic
body:
Redoes PR #507's two EPS import fixes using the PostScript Language Reference (3rd ed.) only. It's stacked on #535; review after it, or only the last two commits. Fixes #498. Part of #505.

**`Fix #498`: an image's several data sources are read in turn**
- The reference has the `image` and `colorimage` operators read multiple data sources in turn, the same amount from each (§4.10 "Images", chapter 8).
- The reader drained each source on its own. When the sources are procedures that read one file a row at a time, the first plane took every component's rows, and the image came out in sheared horizontal bands. That matches #498.
- Fix: one reader, `read_sources`, handles single sources, procedure filters and masked images too.
- Tests in `tests_images.rs`:
  - procedures that read one file, in the dictionary form and the `colorimage` operand form;
  - separate string sources;
  - rows padded to a whole byte at 1, 2, 4, 12 and 16 bits with an odd width;
  - Flate PNG predictors.
- Mutation check: with the old sequential reading, the procedures test fails.

**`Part of #505`: `restore` puts dictionaries back as they were at the `save` (§3.7.3)**
- While a save is open, `def`, `store`, `put`, `undef` and dictionary `copy` keep the old value of each entry they change in a journal, counted against the memory budget.
- `restore` undoes those changes, newest first. Restoring a save that is no longer valid raises `invalidrestore`.
- `cachestatus` now reports a device's cache sizes instead of zeros.
- Test: a program that counts its open saves in a dictionary under a depth limit reads to its end only when `restore` puts the count back. It fails without the journal, and also fails with a zero `cachestatus`.
- #505's reporter sent no file, so this covers what the reference defines, not their specific EPS.

title: Clippy: use as_chunks for constant-size chunks (Rust 1.98)
author: bobtherobot
body:
## What and why

With Rust 1.98 (current stable), clippy's new `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint flags `chunks_exact` with a constant size. Under `-D warnings`, that makes `cargo xtask ci` fail on `main`:

```
error: using `chunks_exact_mut` with a constant chunk size
   --> crates/eps/src/import/data.rs:746:33
```

This switches the four places it flags to `as_chunks`: the EPS stencil-mask loop, the cursor rasterizer's triangle loop, and two cursor tests. `as_chunks` yields fixed-size arrays and, like `chunks_exact`, skips an incomplete last chunk, so behaviour is unchanged. The triangle loop also loses its `let … else { continue }`, which only existed to turn the slice into an array. `as_chunks` has been stable since Rust 1.88, and the workspace's `rust-version` is 1.95.

## How it was tested

- On `main` with Rust 1.98.1, `cargo xtask ci` fails at clippy. With this change, all 7 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, brands, layers, wasm).
- The existing EPS import tests and cursor tests pass. No new test, since nothing behaves differently.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, brands, layers, wasm).
- [x] No panics in shipped code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or
      `unimplemented!` outside tests, and no unchecked indexing on data from files, parameters or
      messages. Errors are returned as `Result` and shown to the user
      ([why and how](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/docs/development.md#robustness-vectorcraft-never-crashes)).
- [x] Clean-room: nothing copied from Adobe products or GPL/AGPL code ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/AGENTS.md)).
- [x] Every new asset has a row in `ASSETS.md` (no new assets).

title: Fix #545: Windows renders through DX12 before Vulkan
author: bflatastic
body:
On Windows every GPU is listed twice, once for Vulkan and once for DX12, and Vulkan came first. On the reporter's Intel GPU, Vulkan made the whole window flicker black while the pointer moved; `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` or `gl` fixed it on the same machine.

- `gpu::adapter_order` now puts a GPU's DX12 adapter before its Vulkan one. This comes after the power preference, so the GPU chosen is the same as before; only the backend that drives it changes.
- Vulkan stays the fallback: if DX12 fails while starting up, the app restarts on Vulkan, and `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` still picks it. Linux, macOS and the web have no DX12 adapter, so nothing changes there.
- Tests: the hybrid-laptop ordering is updated, and a new #545 test covers DX12 first for every preference, plus Vulkan as the next choice when DX12 is skipped.

title: Fix #525: Image Trace of a large photo no longer crashes the app
author: bflatastic
body:
A High Fidelity Photo trace of a 2048 × 2048 photo made 733,000 paths and 7.8 million anchors; the selected result's outlines and anchor squares then built a 1.8 GB egui mesh, over wgpu's largest buffer, and the app quit painting it (after reaching 6.4 GB of memory).

- **Canvas** (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`): a selection with more than 100,000 anchors shows its bounds instead of every outline and anchor square; the hover highlight skips such an object. The Contextual Task Bar and that outline read the selection's bounds from a per-revision cache (`VectorcraftApp::selection_bounds`), so a selected trace draws a frame in ~20 ms instead of ~170 ms.
- **Image Trace** (`crates/trace`): colour layers are traced in parallel with scoped threads (26 s → 1.9 s for that photo; the web build traces them in turn). The new `trace_within` stops once the paths pass an anchor budget; `imageTrace.make` allows 2,000,000 and otherwise fails with "this trace would make more than … anchor points … raise Noise, lower Paths or Colors, or pick a lower-fidelity preset". Images over 64 megapixels are refused from their header, before decoding.
- The trace crate's messages are now in the i18n message scan, with es and it rows.
- Tests: an anchor budget refuses the trace and the full budget equals `trace`; parallel layers keep their order across runs; an oversized PNG header is refused before decoding; a selection past the overlay budget draws its bounds while a normal path still draws its outline and anchors.
- ROADMAP: Image Trace bullet and Last updated.

Tried live in the desktop app with a synthetic 2048² photo: High Fidelity Photo now reports the error in the status bar; Low Fidelity Photo (144k paths, 1.1M anchors) traces, selects, moves and hovers without crashing at ~950 MB.

Not covered: Image Trace still runs on the UI thread (a long trace blocks the window while it runs), and the tracer's edge quality is unchanged.

title: Feat/vectorcraft placed documents
author: Haven-King
body:
## What and why

Place a VectorCraft document in another as a **placed document**: one locked object showing an artboard of the file, linked to it and updated when it changes. Until now, placing a document copied its art in as an editable group, which didn't follow the file and added every copy's paths and resources to the document.

**Breaking change:** `file.place` of a `.vectorcraft` file from a path now links it by default. Pass `link: false` (Place's Link checkbox off) for the editable copy. Placing from `dataBase64` still gives a copy. Files dropped on the canvas follow the same rule (Shift embeds).

- **Links:** check, update, relink, Update Links on open, Link Info (the artboard's size), Placement Options and Edit Original (opens the file in a new tab) work on placed documents. Saving a document in the app updates the open documents that place it.

title: Fix #563: the font menu's live preview no longer flickers
author: bflatastic
body:
A font hovered in a font menu now stays previewed on the selected text instead of switching back and forth every frame.

**Cause:** `font_menu` compared the highlighted row against the `current` font its caller passes. Every caller (Properties, Character panel, Control bar) reads that font from the selected text, which the preview had just changed. One frame later the hovered family looked like the current one, so the menu sent `EndPreview`. The frame after, it sent `Preview` again. The text alternated between the two fonts every frame. On Windows the document's revision climbed by about 100 a second, and the canvas usually showed the original font while the Properties W/H and the font field showed the previewed one.

**Fix:** `MenuState` records the family the text had when the menu opened. The current-row highlight and "back on the current family ends the preview" both use that recorded family.

- Test: `a_preview_stays_put_while_the_menu_is_still` drives the menu the way the panels do, passing the text's font as `current` each frame. Arrow Down previews, six still frames apply nothing, and the document's revision and font stay put. Arrow Up back to the text's family ends the preview. It fails on main (`Some(EndPreview)` on the first still frame).
- ROADMAP Last updated.

Checked live: with "Hello fonts" selected, hovering Stencil in the Properties font menu shows the text in Stencil on the canvas. The revision stays at 4 across seconds; before the fix it reached 1066 within a few seconds of hovering.

title: Fix macOS native menu dismissal
author: mo0kid
body:
## What and why

macOS system menus could remain displayed after selecting an item or clicking back into the window. End AppKit menu tracking on selection, outside window presses and Escape, and consume a dismissal press so it does not also start a canvas gesture.

Defer menu updates while tracking is active, retaining the latest requested state. Apply it after closing the menu and after draining selections against their original item ids. This adapts the reporter-tested fix to the current `mac_menu` backend and preserves its menu layout and shortcut handling.

A separate prerequisite commit fixes an existing Clippy match-guard warning and keeps the leading-model test valid without optional craft-fonts. Upstream already contains the file-URL filter from the original prerequisite commit. Also includes the contributor’s requested opt-in to public GitHub profile-name credit.

title: Fix #569: Shape Builder merges leave no stray edges in their outlines
author: bflatastic
body:
Shape Builder merges now build their outlines from the planar map itself, so merged regions leave no stray lines inside a stroked (unfilled) result.

**Cause:** `shapeBuilder.merge` merged the picked faces with a boolean union of the faces' outlines (`merge_regions`). Each face had been tidied (refit) on its own, so two faces' shared edge could come out a hair apart. The union then kept that edge as a hairline gap between two outlines, or as a spur. What was left of the other shapes was computed by subtracting the merged shape, which could leave slivers along it. With stroke-only art (the rosette of unfilled ellipses in the video) these show up as dangling arcs inside the merged shapes.

- `pathops::FaceMerger` builds the arrangement once per merge and merges any set of faces from it. Faces are picked by their coverage and an interior point, their raw contours are taken from that one topology, and the result is normalised, then tidied with the inputs' curves. Shared edges are exact, so the edges between merged faces vanish. Selections with open paths keep `merge_regions`.
- `shapeBuilder.merge`: the merged shape comes from `FaceMerger`. What is left of each shape is the union of its faces that weren't merged or deleted, instead of the shape minus the merged shape.
- Test `shape_builder_merges_rosette_rings_cleanly`: eight overlapping, unfilled off-centre ellipses, merged by ring drags. It checks that the leftovers don't overlap the merged shape, that no outline is a sliver or carries a spur (it fails on main: an outline 0.53 pt wide on average and 150 pt long, i.e. a spur), and that the merged ring is one outline around the centre.
- ROADMAP Last updated.

On the other points in the issue:
- Hover regions match single faces: `shapeBuilder.regions` gives exactly the 2n(n−1)+1 faces of n rotated ellipses for n = 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12. The larger hatched areas in the video appear to come from regions already merged into one shape, or from drags that touch several faces.

title: Fix #522: SVG round trips keep hidden objects and data-* attributes
author: bflatastic
body:
An SVG animation rig now survives a round trip: hidden alternates stay in the file as `display="none"`, and their `data-*` attributes (pivots) are kept.

- **Hidden objects:** SVG's `hiddenLayers` option now keeps hidden objects as well as hidden layers, each written hidden on its own element (`display="none"` on the path, image, text or group, in every styling mode). The PSD exporter's option of the same name already covered both. `document.save` / Save As sets it unless told otherwise, as before for layers, so **an SVG Save As keeps hidden objects by default**. Plain exports (Export As, `document.export`) still leave them out unless asked. The CLI's `convert` asks, since a conversion keeps the document.
- **`data-*` attributes:** they are kept as the object's own data, in a new `ObjectAttributes.data` field (an ordered list of key/value pairs). It is empty in older files and saved by the native format. Our own `data-name` and `data-vc-*` attributes are left aside.
  - Import keeps them on the objects and layers their elements become, at most 64 per element.
  - Export writes them back.
  - `object.setProps {data: {key: "value" | null}}` sets or removes them. A `data-` prefix on the key is optional, and keys are checked.

  - svg `hidden_objects_and_data_attributes_round_trip` uses the issue's rig plus a lone hidden path. A plain export leaves the hidden objects out. With `hiddenLayers`, in all three styling modes, they are written hidden, are not drawn by resvg, and reopen hidden with all their `data-*`.

title: M7: keep ligatures under small tracking
author: Haven-King
body:
## What and why

Until now any non-zero tracking switched off `liga` and `clig`, even a −5 adjustment made only to fit a line, and it also overrode a `liga` a user might have asked for. Typesetting text sometimes needs small negative tracking, and that costs it its fi/fl ligatures.

- `crates/text/src/features.rs`:
  - Ligatures are suppressed only when |tracking| > 50/1000 em (`LIGATURE_TRACKING_LIMIT`, documented: letterspaced type shouldn't ligate, fitting adjustments should keep ligatures).
  - An explicit `liga`/`+liga`/`clig`/`+clig` in `CharStyle.features` always keeps them. The last ligature tag wins.
  - New public helpers: `ligatures_suppressed_by` and `explicit_ligatures`.
- The OpenType panel's "Ligatures are off while the text is tracked" hint uses the same rule.

## How it was tested

`opentype_ligature_switches` (`crates/text/src/tests_typo.rs`) checks "fi" in Source Serif 4:

| Tracking | Features | Result |
|---|---|---|
| −5, +20, exactly 50 | none | ligature kept |
| ±100 | none | ligature dropped |
| 100 | `liga` or `+liga` | ligature kept |
| 100 | `["liga","-liga"]` | ligature dropped (last tag wins) |
| 0 | `-liga` | ligature dropped |

## Checklist

- [ ] `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, brands, layers, wasm). Run on 0d68c12: fmt, clippy, assets, brands, layers and wasm pass; the test step fails. The only failing test is `cmd::typecmd::area_tests::leading_model_is_set_per_paragraph_and_saved_only_when_top_to_top`, an upstream test that fails the same way on `main` (it depends on the machine's CJK font).
- [x] No panics in shipped code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or

title: Fix #577: the gradient stop popover stays open after the click that opens it
author: bflatastic
body:
The gradient stop's colour popover no longer closes as soon as it opens.

**Cause:** the Gradient panel's "Color:" chip opens the stop popover with a single click, and the popover closes on `clicked_elsewhere()`. The opening click is released in the frame the popover first draws, and the chip is outside the popover, so that click counted as "elsewhere" and closed it in the same frame. A double-click worked because the popover already ignores double-clicks: the one that opens it from a stop on the canvas.

**Fix:** `dialogs/gradient_stop.rs` records the frame the popover first draws in (`__opened`). Only a click in a later frame closes it.

- Test `the_click_that_opens_it_from_the_panel_keeps_it_open`: the press lands before the popover exists and the release in its first frame. It stays open; a later click elsewhere closes it. The test fails on main ("the opening click must not close it"). The dialog-layer test frames now share one `egui::Context`, so frame numbers advance as in the app.
- Existing tests still pass: the canvas double-click opening, Escape, the stop going away.
- ROADMAP Last updated.

Checked live: with the Gradient tool and a stop selected, one click on the Gradient panel's colour chip leaves the popover open. (The canvas double-click opening is covered by the existing test.)

title: M7: Every-line Composer for ragged text
author: Haven-King
body:
The Every-line Composer now breaks ragged (left, centre, right and auto aligned) text as well as justified text, and each text object chooses Single-line or Every-line (`ParaStyle.composer`, Every-line by default as in Illustrator).

## What and why

Illustrator's Every-line Composer balances line breaks over the whole paragraph for ragged text too: it will move a short word down to the next line, even when it fits, to avoid a lone word on the last line and an uneven rag. VectorCraft only composed justified area text, so ragged text always broke greedily. The composer choice wasn't stored, and the Paragraph panel's composer menu items were disabled stubs.

- **Model:** `ParaStyle.composer` (`vectorcraft_doc::Composer`, re-exported by vectorcraft-text). It's saved only when Single-line, so older files read as Every-line. `LayoutOptions.composer` becomes an `Option` override for tests.
- **Composer:**
  - The justified-only gate is gone.
  - Ragged lines never shrink.
  - Badness is `100·r³`, where `r` is the line's leftover space over a rag zone of 1/6 of the width.
  - The last line is free unless it's shorter than 1/3 of the width.
  - Hyphens cost 25 in ragged text (50 in justified).
  - Fitness classes add adjacency demerits.
  - Work is bounded: at most 4,096 active nodes, and greedy breaking above 200k glyphs.
  - Auto alignment counts as ragged.
  - A wrapped line's flush opening bracket (Mojikumi) gives its half em back to the composer.
  - Paragraphs that may hang punctuation (burasagari) keep upstream's line-by-line fallback.
- **Command and UI:** `text.setFormat {composer: "singleLine"|"everyLine"}`. The Paragraph panel menu items work and show a check mark; Reset Panel returns to Every-line.

## How it was tested

- `crates/text/src/tests_typo.rs`:
  - `every_line_composer_balances_ragged_lines`: a word that greedy breaking leaves alone on the last line gets company (Every-line moves the word before it down), in left, centre, right, auto and right-to-left…

title: Fix #578: a drag on the Color panel's spectrum no longer flickers near white
author: bflatastic
body:
Dragging a colour towards white in the Color panel no longer makes the object flicker.

**Cause:** the out-of-gamut and out-of-web warnings under the Color panel's proxy appeared only when the colour needed them, so the panel's height changed with the colour. Along the spectrum's pale top edge, a colour out of the CMYK gamut added a warning row. The spectrum then moved 10 px down under the pointer, the pointer was now above it and picked white, the warning went away and the spectrum moved back up. With the pointer held still, the fill alternated every frame between the pale colour and `#FFFFFF`. A headless probe saw 310 flips in 400 frames. Darker colours don't flicker because they don't toggle the gamut warning.

**Fix:** `panels/color.rs` keeps room, as invisible chips, for the warnings the panel's mode can show (gamut in RGB/HSB, web outside Web Safe RGB and Grayscale). The panel's height now depends on the mode, not the colour. When no warning is showing, RGB mode has about 10 px of empty space under the proxy.

- Test `a_drag_on_the_spectrum_holds_still_near_white`:
  - The panel has one height for white, `#fefefe` (web warning) and `#ded3ff` (both warnings).
  - During a drag along the spectrum's top edge, the fill holds while the pointer stops.
  - It fails on main with heights `[226.375, 226.375, 236.375]`.
- ROADMAP Last updated.

Checked live on Windows:
- The Color panel looks the same with `#DED3FF` (both warnings shown) and `#FFFFFF` (none); the spectrum stays in place.

title: Fix #579: fonts activated by font services such as Adobe Fonts are listed on Windows
author: bflatastic
body:
On Windows, VectorCraft now lists fonts that a font service such as Adobe Fonts activates.

**Cause:** font services load their fonts with GDI at run time, from files in their own folders, without installing them. The font folders and the registry (#443) don't list these fonts, so the font scan never saw them. Since Windows 10 1607, DirectWrite's system font collection includes them. See Microsoft's [What's new in DirectWrite](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/directwrite/what-s-new-in-directwrite-for-windows-8-consumer-preview), "Support for Adobe Typekit and other font-service clients".

- **vectorcraft-text:**
  - New `set_platform_font_files(fn() -> Vec<String>)`: `system_font_dirs` asks the lister again on every scan and every check for installed fonts, so a font activated while the app runs is found the next time the app comes to the front, as in #443.
  - Only files outside the font folders are added, each once (`fonts_outside`).
  - A file named by itself is read whatever its extension. Font services keep fonts in files without one; files found inside a folder still need a font extension.
  - The text crate keeps `forbid(unsafe_code)`.
- **Desktop app (`apps/vectorcraft/src/system_fonts.rs`, Windows except the win7 build):** lists the local files of DirectWrite's system font collection.
  - It uses `IDWriteFactory3::GetSystemFontCollection` with a check for updates, then the font set's face references, file keys and the local font file loader.
  - It goes through the `windows` crate, already in `Cargo.lock` through accesskit, so nothing new is downloaded.
  - The COM calls sit in a scoped `unsafe_code` allowance with SAFETY notes, as `open_documents.rs` does on macOS.
  - Failures (before Windows 10, a non-local font) leave the list as it was; the font count and path length are capped.
  - Fonts are read in place; nothing is copied.

title: Docs: ROADMAP.md one sentence per line, nothing appended to Last updated
author: Haven-King
body:
## What and why

Nearly every PR edits `ROADMAP.md`, and git merges line by line. Two parts of the file made almost any pair of PRs conflict, so each merge forced every open PR to be updated:

- **The "Last updated" line.** Each PR appended its change to it, so it had grown to a single 7,400-character line. All of the last 8 commits that touched `ROADMAP.md` edited it.
- **Paragraph-long lines.** Nine lines were over 2,000 characters. Two PRs that changed different sentences in the same bullet still conflicted.

Changes:

- `ROADMAP.md`:
  - "Last updated" holds only the date and links to "Shipped so far" and the honest assessment.
  - The change list it held moves, word for word, to a new "Changes up to 2026-10-09" section at the end, one item per line. It was the only place in the file that recorded about 67 issue numbers (#319 to #583). The section is closed to new entries and can be deleted if git history and the issues are record enough.
  - Prose (paragraphs and list items) has one sentence per line. The hard-wrapped gap list is joined and re-split by sentence. Sentences over 300 characters also break after each top-level `; ` (outside parentheses, code and links). Tables are unchanged.

    - Keep one sentence per line and never rewrap a paragraph.
    - Don't add your change to "Last updated"; change its date only when the estimates and the assessment are redone as a whole.

title: M7: area type vertical alignment
author: Haven-King
body:
## What and why

Illustrator's Area Type Options can align the lines vertically in the frame. VectorCraft has no vertical alignment, so centering text in a box (labels, buttons, captions, table cells) meant measuring the text and moving the object by hand.

- **Layout** (`crates/text/src/layout.rs`):
  - Each line records its cell (`LineInfo.region`).
  - Center and Bottom shift the lines by the space left in the cell.
  - Justify keeps the first line at the top, puts the last line's descent on the cell bottom, and shares the space left equally between line gaps. There's no paragraph spacing limit; ROADMAP lists it as missing.
  - Non-rectangular frames and text wrap flow again with a top offset until settled. That's at most 8 passes, and text that fit top-aligned is never lost.
  - Vertical type aligns along its block axis.
- **Exports:** they lay the text out again, so SVG, PDF and EPS show the aligned text with no exporter change.
- **Command and UI:** `text.areaOptions {verticalAlign}`. The dialog offers Align and First Baseline as dropdowns through the parameter dialog's choices table.

title: M7: area type auto size and shrink text to fit
author: Haven-King
body:
## What and why

Area type that didn't fit could only overflow, and nothing outside the text crate could tell that it had. Illustrator's Auto Size was missing, even though its preference existed and did nothing. Templates with fixed boxes and variable text (labels, data-driven layouts) need text that shrinks to fit, which until now meant re-running layout by hand or in a script.

- **Model:** `AreaOptions.fit`: `none` (default, not saved), `"autoHeight"`, or `{"shrinkText": {"minPercent": N}}` (10–100, default 50).
- **Shrink Text to Fit:**
  - Runs at layout time, so render and every export see it.
  - Searches whole tenths of a point of the first run's size, so the result is exactly the largest 0.1 pt step that fits.
  - Scales sizes, explicit leading and baseline shift; paragraph spacing stays.
  - `TextLayout.fit_scale` records the factor.
- **Auto Size:**
  - Resolved in `refresh_bounds` inside each text edit, so the resize shares the edit's undo step.
  - Applies to rectangular, horizontal, single-row frames; columns get the least height that holds the text.
  - A hand-set height or threading turns it off.
  - The Auto Size New Area Type preference now gives new area type Auto Size.
- **Reporting:** `text.areaOptions` and `document.inspect` / `document.node {summary}` report `overflow`, `fit` and `fitScale`.
- **UI:** the Area Type Options dialog offers Fit as a dropdown (None, Auto Size, Shrink Text to Fit).

## How it was tested

- `crates/text/src/tests_fit.rs`:
  - The text fits, and 0.1 pt larger overflows (one and two columns).
  - The minimum percentage is respected; no change when the text already fits; leading scales.
  - Point and on-path type ignore the fit; degenerate sizes are handled.
  - Works with Top-to-Top leading and Character Alignment.
- `crates/engine/src/tests_areafit.rs`:

title: Fix #592: file dialogs on Linux no longer stop the window answering
author: bflatastic
body:
On Linux, a file dialog left open no longer makes the compositor offer to kill VectorCraft as not responding.

**Cause:** VectorCraft's file dialogs (Open, Save As, Export, Place, presets, Relink, folder pickers) were synchronous `rfd::FileDialog` calls on the UI thread. The app asks for a path and continues with it right away.
- On Windows and macOS the native dialog keeps the window's events running while it is open.
- On Linux nothing answered the Wayland `xdg_wm_base` ping, so Hyprland showed "Application not responding" after about 4.5 s.
- No parent window was passed either, so the portal logged "Unhandled parent window type".

**Fix:**
- **ui-egui `picks`:** every file dialog (open, open several, save, folder) now goes through one module. All about 20 call sites are routed through it.
  - When the host provides `Services::start_pick`, the dialog runs on its own thread. What asked for it gives up for now. When the dialog answers, that *entry* runs again and gets the picked path immediately. An entry is one of:
    - a command (`app.run`, outermost call),
    - a dialog's OK (`dialogs::confirm`, on the dialog as it was),
    - a panel's or dialog body's button (Relink, Relink to Folder, Unembed, Asset Export, the Export for Screens and Package folder buttons, the presets dialogs' Import).
  - "cancelled" isn't shown while the dialog is open. Asking for a second dialog meanwhile says one is already open (new string, translated in cs, es, it, ja, pt-br, ru, zh-hans and zh-hant).
- **Desktop app:**
