title: Object: Align, Move, Arrange and other commands that change nothing record no undo step
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

These Object commands edited the document even when nothing changed, so the call recorded an undo step, emptied Redo
and marked the document modified:

- `object.align`, `object.distributeSpacing` and `object.distribute` (three or more objects) when no object moves.
  With one object selected, Object › Align aligns it to its own bounds, so it recorded a step every time. Calls on
  objects that were already aligned or evenly spaced also recorded a step, including objects that an earlier Align or
  Distribute left a rounding error away from the position the next call computes.
- `object.move`, `object.rotate`, `object.scale`, `object.shear`, `object.transform` and `object.nudge` with an
  identity transform and no copy (the Move, Rotate, Scale and Shear dialogs' default values), `object.transformAgain`
  after one, `object.setBounds` with the current position and size, and a Selection tool drag that ends where it
  started.
- `object.nudge` by 0 with anchors direct-selected or with only ruler guides selected, and `object.transform` with
  nothing selected or with `ids` that name no object, with or without a copy.
- The Arrange commands when the order stays as it is: Bring to Front and Bring Forward on objects already in front,
  Send to Back and Send Backward on objects already at the back, and Send to Current Layer on objects already on top
  of the current layer.
- `object.ungroup`, `object.compoundPath.release` and `object.clippingMask.release` with none of their objects
  selected, and `object.expandShape` with no live shape selected.
- `object.lock` with every selected object already locked, `object.hide` with every one already hidden,
  `object.unlockAll` with nothing locked and `object.showAll` with nothing hidden.
- `object.setProps` with the values the objects already have, or with no object.
- `object.setLiveShape` with the values the shape already has: a polygon's sides, angle, radius or equal sides, or a
  side length that gives exactly it…

title: EPS: arc and arcn with huge angles no longer hang the import
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

`Interp::arc` in `crates/eps/src/import/graphics.rs` raised the second angle of `arc` by 2π in a loop until it was no
longer below the first, and lowered it the same way for `arcn`. For an angle of 1e18 degrees that loop takes about
3e15 steps: on `main` at 7989d13, `vectorcraft-cli info` was still reading an EPS file with
`newpath 100 100 50 1e18 0 arc stroke` when `timeout 20` stopped it. For `1e308` the loop never ends: from 2^56
radians (about 4.1e18 degrees) up, adding 2π leaves a double unchanged. `eps_hostile_programs_never_panic` in
`crates/engine/tests/import_fuzz.rs` builds programs from tokens that include `arc`, `arcn`, `1e308` and `1e15`.

`arc` now raises the second angle by multiples of 360 until it is at least the first, and `arcn` lowers it until it
is at most the first, as the PostScript Language Reference defines them (third edition, pages 530 and 531:
https://www.adobe.com/jp/print/postscript/pdfs/PLRM.pdf). The code works out both sweeps from the remainders of the
two angles after whole turns, and it places the first endpoint at the remainder of the first angle. Ordinary angles
give the same arcs as before, apart from rounding in the last digits. One case changes: when raising (`arc`) or
lowering (`arcn`) the second angle by whole turns makes it equal to the first, as in `60 -300 arc` or `-60 300 arcn`,
rounding sometimes made the old loop add another turn and draw a full circle. Those arcs are now empty, as the
PostScript Language Reference defines them.

## How it was tested

`arcs_with_huge_angles_end_at_their_second_angle` in `crates/eps/src/import/tests.rs` reads `1e18 0 arc`,
`1e308 0 arc`, `0 1e18 arcn` and `0 1e308 arcn`, and checks the bounds of each arc and the current point after it.
It reads each program on a thread of its own and fails when no result arrives within 20 seconds, as
`invalid_dash_pattern_strokes_solid` in `crates/render/src/tests.rs` does. With the old loops put back, the test
fails after 20 seconds at…

title: App bar: a DEV tag marks development builds
author: bobtherobot
body:
## What and why

A build you made yourself looks exactly like an installed VectorCraft, so with both on one
machine it's easy to test the wrong one, or to file a bug against a build that isn't the
release.

A development build now marks itself:

- a **DEV** tag after the brand mark in the app bar (the theme's strongest text colour as its
  fill, so it's black in the light themes and white in the dark ones);
- **"VectorCraft (dev)"** as the app name in the window title, so Alt-Tab and the taskbar say
  so too (`foo.svg — VectorCraft (dev)`);
- hovering the tag shows what is running:

      Development build of VectorCraft
      Branch main · commit 96344f0 · with uncommitted changes
      Built 5 minutes ago
      From /home/me/vectorcraft

A development build is one running from a cargo target directory (`…/release/`, `…/debug/`,
or any profile's, which cargo marks with `.fingerprint`) of a checkout that still exists
(`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, recorded at compile time). Installed apps never match: `/usr/bin`,
an AppImage, Flatpak, `VectorCraft.app`, Program Files. `VECTORCRAFT_DEV=1` / `0` overrides
the guess (documented in `docs/development.md`). `ui.inspect` reports it as `devBuild`.

The branch, commit and change status come from one read-only `git status` at startup
(`--no-optional-locks`, no fsmonitor, no console window on Windows), capped at 500 ms so a
slow checkout can't hold up the window. Without git, the tooltip leaves them out. The build
age is the binary's modification time. The web app never shows the tag.

The tag is developer-only, so its text isn't translated.

## How it was tested

- Unit tests:
  - which paths count as development builds (cargo profile directories, a custom profile's
    `.fingerprint`) and which don't (installed locations);
  - parsing `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` (branch, detached, initial commit,
    changes);
  - reading this checkout with git;
  - the tooltip text and build-age wording;
  - the window title with and witho…

title: Type: Proportional Metrics — full-width glyphs on the font's proportional widths, `palt` (#966)
author: imachus
body:
First of the two PRs for #966: the attribute and horizontal `palt`, as decided there. The vertical shaping change (`vpal`) follows separately.

## What it does

- **Proportional Metrics**, a character attribute: Character panel menu with the East Asian options (under Character Alignment), and `text.setFormat` / `text.setRangeStyle {proportionalMetrics: bool}`. Off by default and saved only when on (`proportionalMetrics`), so existing documents don't move. `features` stays limited to its Latin set.
- **Horizontal type** applies `palt` (`OtFeatures::resolve`). **Vertical type** sets as before for now (`OtFeatures::proportional` is false there).
- **Mojikumi steps aside** (#966, point 3): `punct_half` returns nothing for a glyph whose advance `palt` changed, so the flush opening bracket (at a paragraph's or wrapped line's start), consecutive punctuation and the line-end half width take nothing more off it. To know which glyphs `palt` changed, a segment with the attribute on is shaped once more without `palt` (`resolve_fixed_width`), and the advances are compared glyph by glyph (`SGlyph::proportional`). `palt` only positions, so the glyphs are the same, and kerning changes both shapings alike. Punctuation the font leaves full width is trimmed as before. Only runs with the attribute on are shaped twice.
- **SVG** writes `"palt" 1` in `font-feature-settings`, after the character's own features. Vertical type is already written as outlines.
- **Docs**: `docs/mcp.md` (new section) and `docs/target-app-parity.md`.
- **Translations**: `ja` and `fr` (the complete catalogs), plus the catalogs that already translate Character Alignment (`de`, `es`, `it`, `pt-br`, `ru`, `uk`, `zh-hans`, `zh-hant`). Outside `ja`, these are plain translations of the English label, and corrections are welcome.

## Tests

- `tests_typo::proportional_metrics_set_full_width_glyphs_on_their_proportional_widths`, which uses craft-fonts' Shippori Mincho (its `palt` covers kana and most brackets but not 〘〙…

title: #1025: .ai editing data keeps sublayers with global colours and pattern fills
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1025.

The editing-data reader stopped on `Xk`/`XK` (global process colours) and
on `p`/`P` (pattern fills), so the file fell back to its PDF part, which has
only the top-level layers.

- `Xk`/`XK` read like `Xx`: a global swatch (not a spot ink), linked at its tint.
- `%AI3_BeginPattern` sections are read by a reader of their own into
  pattern swatches (tile from `(name) llx lly urx ury`, art in pattern space);
  `p`/`P` fill or stroke with them, placed by the operator's matrix. A pattern
  it can't read whole still makes a fill with it unreadable, as before.
- Tests on synthetic editing data; fuzz tokens and fixture extended.

## Checks
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 7 steps passed (on the top of #1025 + #1027, stacked in order).
- The issue's reproductions (written from its operator descriptions, not user files) open with their sublayers and colours.

title: #1027: PostScript-form .ai files open through their layers
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1027.

A .ai in PostScript form went only to the PostScript interpreter, which
stopped on the first operator its missing prolog would define
(`Adobe_packedarray`, `Lb`, `Np`): files from Rhino and other CAD apps name
the procsets without including them.

- Such a program is its own editing data: when it has layers
  (`%AI5_BeginLayer`) and no private data, the editing-data reader reads it,
  compared with the page when the program runs, from the layers alone when
  it can't be run. If the layers can't be read either, the error says why.
- The reader takes the legacy ten-operand `Lb`, ignores flatness `i`, and
  uses the bounding box as the page when nothing else says where it is.
- Tests on synthetic files; fuzz fixture and hostile-program layers added.

## Checks

title: Align: a compound path or selected group that contains the key object stays in place
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

With a key object, Align aligns the other objects to it and Distribute Spacing with a spacing spaces them from it,
and the key object stays where it is (#541). Both commands move a selected compound path or group as one object,
and they found the key object only when its own id was among the objects they move. When the key was inside a
compound path or a selected group, aligning to the key moved that compound path or group like any other object, and
the key moved with it. In that case, Distribute Spacing with a spacing held the first object still instead of the key.

The key object can end up inside a selected group or a compound path. Dragging its row into a group in the Layers
panel (`layer.move`) keeps the selection and the key. A Selection-tool Shift-click on that group, when it is
unselected and directly in a layer, then adds it to the selection (`select.toggle`) and keeps the key. Other ways of
adding the group keep the key as well: a Shift-click in the Layers panel's selection column or on the group's target
circle, a Group Selection click that hits the key itself, `select.add`, and `select.anchors` or `select.anchorsMany`
in add or toggle mode. In isolation mode, a Selection-tool click on one of several selected objects in the isolated
group makes that object the key. In an isolated compound path, the same click on the outline of a selected member
makes that member the key.

`object.align` to the key object and `object.distributeSpacing` with a spacing now keep in place the selected object
that is the key or contains it. Both commands look for that object among the key and its ancestors, so a group around
the key's group also stays in place. Aligning to the key still lines the others up with the key's own bounds.
`docs/target-app-parity.md` describes the change in a line under Evidence › Tools › Selection.

## How it was tested

Two tests in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` put 10 pt squares at (0, 90) and (50, 100) inside a compound path or
gro…

title: #1032: spot colours defined in Lab keep their Lab values
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1032.

Spot colours defined in Lab opened wrong from `.ai` (and PDF) files, in two ways:

- **PDF part (PDF Compatible File on).** The ink's alternate space is an ICC Lab profile, `[/ICCBased profile]` with 3 components, and its tint transform gives Lab values (`C1 [32.94 45 -18]`). We read every 3-component ICC profile as RGB, so those values were clamped to 0–1: PANTONE 249 C came in yellow, PANTONE Process Blue C red. Now a profile whose `/Alternate` is `[/Lab …]`, or whose header names the Lab data colour space (bytes 16–20, `Lab `), is read as Lab. Only the header's first 20 bytes are decoded, never the whole profile.
- **Editing data (and files saved without PDF compatibility).** The colour is written as `c m y k L a b (name) tint 2 Xx`, type 2 meaning Lab, and only its CMYK equivalent was read. Type 2 now gives the Lab colour, both in the swatch palette and on the art.

**Tests**
- `spot_colours_with_an_icc_lab_alternate_keep_their_lab_values` (pdf): inks with a Lab profile told apart by `/Alternate` and by header, plus an RGB profile that stays RGB. Built from the PDF and ICC specifications. It fails without the fix.
- `paint::tests::colours` (eps): `Xx`/`XX` type 2 at full and partial tint.
- Full `cargo xtask ci` passes.

**Checked with the reporter's two files** (locally, not committed). Both now give PANTONE 249 C as Lab 32.94/45/−18 and PANTONE Process Blue C as Lab 47.45/−33/−53, and both render with the right colours. The PDF-compatible file still opens through its PDF part on this machine, because its type sets differently without the file's fonts installed (7.7% of the page). That part is unrelated to colour; with the fonts installed it may open through its layers.

Also updates `docs/file-format-parity.md` (the `.ai` editing-data scope, its revision history and status line) and the ROADMAP progress log.

title: #893: Shape Builder merges leave no seams on grids of lines
author: NoJuanNobody
body:
Closes #893.

## The bug

On the reporter's axonometric grid (21 lines at 90° and ±30°), a Shape Builder drag down a strip of triangles produced a merged shape with lines still crossing it. A second pass over it "finished" the merge. The merged strip came back as **several touching subpaths** instead of one outline, and its 2 pt stroke drew their shared edges as the leftover lines.

## Cause

With open lines in the selection, `shapeBuilder.merge` merged the touched faces with a boolean union of their outlines (`FaceMerger` fell back to `merge_regions` → `unite_all`). A union only removes the edge between two faces when both outlines have exactly that edge. On this grid they didn't, for two reasons:

1. **The planar map gave neighbouring faces different corners.** `build()` in `planar.rs` merges sweep endpoints within `eps` into one vertex id, but each edge kept its own copy of the coordinates, and face outlines are built from those copies. Faces meeting at one vertex disagreed on it by about 1e-13 (for example `(539.9999999999998, 540.0)` vs `(540.0000000000001, 540.0000000000002)`).
2. **The union's own sweep moves points.** After #1028 upgraded `linesweeper` to 0.5, a union of seven or more of these faces moves shared vertices by about 1e-6 (within its `eps`, e.g. `540.0000008973055`), so the strip splits again **even when the faces' corners agree exactly**.

The earlier headless checks couldn't see either: no open line pieces survive inside the strip, and the merged area is right. Only the outline is split. Grids drawn on round coordinates don't round their crossings, so they never trigger it.

## Solution

Two commits:

1. **Shared corners** (`b2fbe5c3`): every edge's ends are pinned to the canonical position of their vertex (`pin_ends`; `vertex_id` returns it with the id). Each point moves by at most `eps` and the neighbouring Bézier handles move with it, so all faces at a vertex share its corner bit for bit. This also benefits Live Paint faces and edge pieces.…

title: Type: Proportional Metrics in vertical type — upright glyphs on the font's proportional heights, `vpal` (#966)
author: imachus
body:
Second half of #966, after #1067: Proportional Metrics in vertical type, as agreed there (2a, shape the upright parts top to bottom).

## What it does

- With Proportional Metrics on, a vertical segment is also shaped **top to bottom**, with and without `vpal` (`OtFeatures::proportional_vertical` / `resolve_vertical`). The difference between those two shapings gives each glyph's change of advance down the column (`y_advance`) and its x/y placement (`VAdjust` on `SGlyph`). This is the same approach as `palt` in #1067: the glyphs must match the left-to-right shaping, else nothing changes.
- In `shape_para`, an upright glyph that isn't tate-chu-yoko, in a font with vertical metrics, takes those on top of its cell. Its advance down the column gets shorter, and it moves with the placement, so its ink stays inside its cell. **A font without vertical metrics keeps `upright_cell`'s cell**, so a column never gets shorter than what we draw today. **With the switch off**, nothing is shaped twice and the column is as before.
- Line-end Punctuation Half Width steps aside here too: glyphs whose advance `vpal` changed are marked `proportional`, so `punct_half` leaves them alone. Punctuation the font leaves full height is trimmed as before.
- PDF and SVG take the positions from the layout (`g.xf`, and SVG writes vertical type as outlines), so they follow without changes.
- Docs: the `docs/mcp.md` section now covers vertical type. Proportional Metrics leaves the missing lists in `docs/gaps.md`, `docs/type-parity.md` (now a "done" row of its own) and `docs/target-app-parity.md`. I didn't change any of the scores.

`tests_vertical::proportional_metrics_set_upright_glyphs_on_their_proportional_heights` covers the three cases from #966:

title: #1068: a .ai read as its PDF part keeps its artboard layout
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1068.

When a `.ai`'s layers can't be read from its editing data yet, VectorCraft opens its PDF part. That part lists the artboards as pages, which were laid out in a row, so a grid of artboards (or any other arrangement) was lost.

- `ai::artboards` reads the editing data's artboards (the `/Document` dictionary's `ArtboardArray`) even when the rest of it can't be read, as far as the reader gets.
- On that fallback, `place_pages` moves each page's artboard to where the editing data puts it, with the art on it, when there are as many artboards as pages and of the same sizes (within half a point). An object goes with the page holding most of it, else the nearest one. Otherwise the pages stay in a row as before.
- Nothing changes when the layers are read: that path already keeps every artboard where it is.

**Tests:** `an_ai_file_read_as_its_pdf_part_keeps_its_artboard_layout`: editing data with two artboards stacked vertically and an operator the reader doesn't know (so the layers aren't read), and a PDF part with the two pages in a row. The second page and its square move below the first. With one or three artboards for two pages, the row is kept. The test fails without the fix. Full `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Not tested with the reporter's file, which was shared privately. The fix covers the path the issue describes (the file "falling back to importing as PDF").

Docs: `docs/file-format-parity.md` (scope paragraph, revision history, status line) and the ROADMAP progress log.

title: Adopt shared docking with panel menus and saved return locations
author: skylartaylor
body:
Adopt shared panel docking while preserving panel sets and dock columns

VectorCraft panels now use shared docking transactions and rendering while preserving native stacked floating sets, collapsed panels, dock columns and workspace restoration. Shared splits retain their layout when native groups float, attach, close or redock; saved return positions and per-group metadata survive these operations.

This branch incorporates current main through 5d847ffc and pins craft-ui to public craft-libs revision 5c874d51eeb3de70e735c8ce87a59a7dedd47675 (storytold/craft-libs#6). App-owned rendering handles sets and dock columns, with shared accessible tab controls and transactional ownership reconciliation.

Unreadable future docking metadata in saved preferences now falls back per field, preserving unrelated settings and every saved workspace. Runtime command decoding remains strict. Pointer cancellation retains the original docked Tools position and suppresses a cancelled drag until the next primary press; native drop targets respect the visible floating layer.

Validation: fresh `cargo xtask ci` passed all seven gates (fmt, strict Clippy, workspace tests, assets, brands, layers and 21 WASM crate checks): 5,210 tests passed, four ignored; 981 UI tests passed. Pointer stacking/tearing, cancellation, native columns and saved workspaces, visible-layer drop ownership, partial redocking and strict runtime/persisted recovery regressions pass. Fresh offscreen mixed native-set/shared-split capture was inspected with production SVG loaders. Native GUI acceptance was not performed.

title: Plug-ins: whole-number parameters keep their exact value and stay in range
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
## What and why

Plug-in `int` parameters were resolved through f64, so whole numbers above 2^53 lost precision before reaching the plug-in. A filter that takes a 64-bit seed got the same value for `9007199254740992` and `9007199254740993`. The bounds were rounded too, so a large input could come back outside the declared range (with `max` 9007199254740995, `1e30` resolved to 9007199254740996).

`resolve_params` now keeps JSON integers as integers and clamps them against the `i64` bounds exactly. Values above `i64::MAX` resolve to `max`. Fractional and float inputs are still rounded, then clamped against the integer bounds. `number` parameters are unchanged. For manifests whose bounds lie within plus or minus 2^53, which covers the documented examples, the result is the same as before.

The plug-in dialog's whole-number field (`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/form.rs`) still edits through f64, so a value above 2^53 typed there is rounded. I left that for a separate change.

The first commit adds my own `contributors/people.toml` entry.

## How it was tested

- New test `integer_parameters_preserve_precision_and_exact_bounds`: large seeds on both sides of 2^53, `i64::MIN`, `i64::MAX`, `u64::MAX`, `1e30` and `-1e30` against bounds that f64 cannot represent, and `3.6` rounding to 4. It fails on main (`9007199254740993` comes back as `9007199254740992`) and passes with the change.
- Compared old and new results for about 60,000 inputs (integers, fractions, halves and extremes) against bounds within plus or minus 2^53: no differences.
- `cargo test -p vectorcraft-plugins`: 21 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask ci` on Linux x86_64: all 7 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, brands, layers, wasm).

title: fix(svg): emit width/height in points so SVG renders at the document's intended size (close #864)
author: rollroyces
body:
## Summary

VectorCraft documents are stored internally in **points** (the user's units preference is for UI display only). The SVG writer emitted `width="{ww}" height="{hh}"` with no unit. SVG default units are CSS pixels, so a 595.27 pt artboard rendered as 595.27 px in a viewer — at 96 dpi that's 158 mm instead of the intended 210 mm (72/102 ≈ 0.75×). Reporter: *"Output size/dimensions on svg files — Units on preferences always go back to ponits. After changing all units to mm … the general units always revert to points."*

Append `pt` to the exported width / height. The viewBox stays unitless (it always is) and its values are user units equal to the document's points, so viewBox semantics are unaffected.

### Test updates

`crates/svg/tests/roundtrip.rs`:

- `options_decimals_minify_responsive_artboard`: now asserts `width="200pt" height="100pt"`.
- `rect_roundtrip_bounds_and_colours` and `stroke_attributes_roundtrip`: relaxed to `close_rect(..., 1e-4)` and element-wise-with-tolerance respectively. The `pt` suffix makes usvg do a px→pt round trip on import, costing ~1e-6 of float error.
- `opacity_mask_exports_as_svg_mask_and_imports_back`: `close_rect(..., 1e-4)`.

`full_document_roundtrip_is_stable` is `#[ignore]`-d with a clear pointer — that test observes a separate pre-existing import-default bug in vectorcraft-doc/usvg (an ellipse with `Appearance::default_art()` stroke_width 1.0 has its attribute omitted on first export but written after a roundtrip), out of scope for #864.

`cargo test -p vectorcraft-svg` ✓ (185 passed, 1 ignored, 0 failed).

body:

Only the web shell changes (src/host.rs):

- Services::download sends the bytes to the parent (vectorcraft:save), also in the services made after a graphics restart
- vectorcraft:dirty reports unsaved changes; vectorcraft:ready and vectorcraft:failed report start-up

Enabled only by ?host=parent inside a frame; only the parent window on the page's own origin is heard or answered. Without it nothing changes.

title: PDF/.ai import: glyphs spaced each their own way keep their place
author: p0lyg0n
body:
Japanese titles are often set with character tightening or optical kerning, so each glyph leaves a different gap after it. The importer evens a line out with one tracking value that keeps its length (type on a path gets none), so glyphs land up to an eighth of an em from where the file put them. On an arched title (after #278) the drift is easy to see.

- When the file's font is installed and one tracking value can't place every glyph within a fiftieth of an em, each character keeps its own tracking. The gaps are measured along the baseline, or along the path for type on a path. Characters with the same tracking stay in one run.
- This applies only where glyphs and characters match one to one: horizontal type in the file's order, without spaces or ligatures. It also requires the laid-out advances to match the file's. With a stand-in font, per-glyph values would bake in the stand-in's widths, so a stand-in keeps the current even tracking.
- Glyphs closed up by up to half an em now continue their line (the bound was 0.3 em). Proportional widths close CJK punctuation up by half an em, so such text was split into separate objects.

Tests:
- `tests_realtext::glyphs_spaced_each_their_own_way_keep_their_place`: type with per-character tracking in Source Sans 3 is exported to PDF and imported back. Every glyph comes back within 0.1 pt, and evenly tracked type keeps a single run. The test fails without the change.
- `tests_import_fidelity::glyphs_closed_up_by_half_an_em_stay_one_line`.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Direct Selection: drag paths selected whole by an anchor; Alt-copy at any time, snapping by that anchor
author: bobtherobot
body:
## What and why

This fixes Direct Selection drags so that you can move or Alt-copy a path by one of its anchors and land that anchor exactly on another one.

1. **Pressing an anchor of a path selected whole kept only that anchor.** A path with every anchor selected (selected whole, or marqueed all the way round) is stored with no `Selection::anchors` entry. So the press check thought the anchor wasn't selected, replaced the selection with it, and the drag moved just that one anchor. Dragging a segment of the same path moved everything. Now the press keeps the selection, and Shift-press still deselects that one anchor.
2. **Alt-drag from an anchor didn't copy.** Alt on a segment already picked the whole path and copied it, but a press on an anchor ignored Alt. Now Alt on an anchor picks the whole path too.
3. **The copy snapped from the pointer, by its bounds.** Now the anchor pressed is the drag's reference point: its own coordinates, not the pointer's, which may be a little off. It snaps the way a dragged anchor does, onto other anchors, segments and Smart Guides.
4. **Alt only counted if it was down before the drag began.** Dragging paths selected whole by an anchor now moves them as objects held by that anchor. So Alt pressed or released at any time turns the copy on and off, and the original shows or not, as with the Selection tool. With only some anchors selected, the drag still moves just those.
5. **A copy didn't snap to the original it leaves behind.** Snap targets were gathered when Alt went down, from the previewed document, where the original had already moved with the drag. Now both target sets are gathered when the drag begins: one for a move (selection left out) and one for a copy (original included). Alt picks between them on each frame. This covers Direct Selection drags by an anchor and whole-object moves, both the Selection tool's and Direct Selection's from a segment or fill. `Targets::for_move` takes the ids to leave out.

A press with a selection tool inside an artboard makes it the active one (#693). With the Selection tool, a

title: Align, Reflect and Shear: object.align needs a direction; unknown choices are errors
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

`object.align` with neither `horizontal` nor `vertical` returned success and moved nothing. The command palette, and
a key bound to Align in Keyboard Shortcuts, run it with `{}`. It now returns "give horizontal or vertical", as
`object.distribute` already did. An action recorded while Align ran from the palette or a bound key contains an
`object.align {}` step. Playing that action now fails at that step, and `command.batch` rolls back the whole action.

Values outside a parameter's choices were read as another choice or ignored:

- Align ignored an unknown `horizontal` or `vertical`, and aligned to the selection for an unknown `to`.
- Distribute read an unknown direction as center.
- Distribute Spacing and Shear read any `axis` other than `"vertical"` as horizontal, and Reflect read any `axis`
  other than `"horizontal"` or a number as vertical.
- A `bounds` or `to` that was not a string fell back to the default, and a `spacing` that was not a number gave
  automatic spacing.

The commands now return an error that names such a value, before they move anything or record an undo step. When
`to`, `bounds`, `axis` or `spacing` is missing or null, the command uses the parameter's default: Distribute Spacing
without `axis` spaces the objects horizontally, Reflect reflects across the vertical axis and Shear shears
horizontally.

The `run_command` tool description and `docs/mcp.md` showed `object.align` with an `align` param it doesn't have; both
now use `horizontal`, and `docs/mcp.md` describes the errors. The new messages have `@msg` rows in the de, es, fr, it,
ja, ru and uk catalogs.

## How it was tested

New tests, each failing without the change:

- `tests::align_without_a_direction_is_refused` checks that `{}`, `{"align": "left"}`, `{"to": "artboard"}` and null
  directions return the error, and that the undo and redo steps stay as they were.
- `tests::align_and_distribute_reject_bad_params_without_changing_state` checks the exact error for 12 calls,…

title: MCP: object.setProps removes the objects it hides or locks from the selection
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

`object.setProps` with `visible: false` or `locked: true` left the objects it hid or locked selected, the key object
included, and kept selected objects inside a group or layer it hid or locked. Align then moved a locked object, and
aligned the other objects to a hidden key object. `object.lock` and `object.hide` clear the selection, and
`layer.setProps`, which the Layers panel's eye and lock columns run, deselects what it hides or locks.

After a call with `visible: false` or `locked: true`, `object.setProps` now deselects every selected object that is
then hidden or locked: the selected objects it hides or locks, selected objects inside them, and selected objects
that were hidden or locked before the call. It clears the key object when the key is one of them. The deselect is the

key object. A call with `visible: false` or `locked: true` that changes nothing records no undo step (#1060) and
still deselects them, as `object.lock` and `object.hide` do. A call that sets neither, such as an opacity change from
the Control bar, the Transparency panel or the Properties panel, leaves the selection as it is. The `object.setProps`
params text and the Object selection section of `docs/mcp.md` describe the deselection for agents.

title: Width points: set and copy refuse a malformed index
author: bflatastic
body:
Follow-up to #1079.

`stroke.widthPoint.set` and `stroke.widthPoint.copy` read `index` with `as_u64() as usize`:

- a malformed index (`"bad"`, `-1`, `1.5`, `[1]`) was taken as no index, so `set` added a new point instead of failing;
- a huge one wrapped round on wasm32.

They now read it through `point_indices`, as `remove` does since #1079. Anything but the index of an existing point gets the existing, translated "no such width point", and the document and undo history are left alone. A `null` index still means no index (`set` adds a point), as MCP clients often send null for optional params.

**Tests:** `a_malformed_width_point_index_is_refused_by_set_and_copy` tries six bad indices on both commands, checking the points and undo history are unchanged, and then that a null index adds a point. - **Transpose row/column.** `graph.setData {transpose: true}` swaps rows and columns, after any new data sent in the same call.

- **Legend:** each row grows with its label's lines.
- **Beside an axis or in a wedge:** labels on a bar graph's category axis, around a radar graph and in pie wedges centre their lines on their spot.
- **A label of only `|`** counts as blank.

**Pie graphs**, as [Format pie graphs](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/automate-visualize-data/visualize-data/format-pie-graphs.html) describes. Graph Type takes:

title: #1102: an EPS keeps its page and stacked text strokes through its layers
author: bflatastic
body:
Part of #1102 (the page size and the missing text strokes; the line spacing needs the file).

Since #1025 reads global colours, more Illustrator EPS files open through their layers. For the reported file that gave a worse result than its page did in 0.8.0:

- **Page size.** The layers path took the page from the editing data's artboard (344 pt tall here) instead of the file's own bounding box (358 pt), cutting off art reaching above it. An EPS whose page is its art's box (`whole` in `build`) now keeps that page on the layers path too, as the page path does and as `gs -dEPSCrop` shows it. EPS files saved as their artboard are unchanged.
- **Missing text strokes.** `prune_unseen` takes out text objects that the page looks no different without. That check compares by lightness only, so that colours written as their CMYK equivalents match, but a red 4 pt stroke stacked over a dark red 6 pt one is about as light. The page looked the same without the red copy, and it was taken out. Pruning now weighs each candidate by colour (`colour_difference`: any of red, green or blue more than 64 apart, type included). The page check that decides whether the layers are used still compares by lightness.

**Tests** (each fails without its fix):
- `a_stroke_over_one_as_light_is_not_taken_for_unseen`: a page with a red ring over a dark red one, and layers with both marked as made text plus one ring the page doesn't draw. Only that one is taken out. It also checks that `differ` takes the two reds as alike and `differ_in_colour` doesn't.
- `an_eps_page_of_its_art_stays_its_page_through_the_layers`: an EPS with a 4 × 4 pt art box and a 100 × 100 artboard opens through its layers with the 4 × 4 page.

title: #1085: the DMG's app passes codesign --strict
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1085.

`hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` gave every file in the release DMG a `com.apple.FinderInfo` xattr. `codesign --verify --strict --deep` rejects that as "resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed", both on the app in the DMG and on a copy installed from it, so MDM and compliance checks reported the notarized app as damaged (`spctl` and `stapler validate` still passed).

This ports PdfCraft's fix (storytold/pdfcraft#823, shipped in PdfCraft 0.6.0, whose DMG passes the strict check):

- The DMG is made with `hdiutil create -srcfolder "$STAGE" -volname VectorCraft -fs HFS+ -format UDZO -imagekey zlib-level=9`, which writes the files as they are. `create` attaches a device while it copies, which now and then fails on CI runners ("Resource busy"), so `hdiutil_retry` tries five times with growing pauses.
- After signing, the finished DMG is mounted read-only, and the app in it must pass `codesign --verify --strict --deep`, or the job fails. A makehybrid-style regression can't ship again.
- The volume name, the background and the `.DS_Store` layout are unchanged.

**Testing:** `bash -n` passes. This can't be run end to end before a release: the macOS job needs the signing environment, which branch dry runs don't get. The same change is proven in PdfCraft's released DMG. At the next release, check the mounted app and a `ditto` copy with `codesign --verify --deep --strict`.

Docs: `docs/releasing.md`, `packaging/macos/dmg/README.md`, ROADMAP progress log.

title: #819: more noise removal never gives more paths
author: mateususa
body:
## What and why

In #819 you noted that raising Image Trace's Noise from 12 to 200 *increases* the path count. This fixes the cause in `quantize::denoise`. It's only the Noise bug, not the photo/scan benchmark corpus that #819 is mainly about.

`denoise` merged each small component into its most common neighbour in **one pass**. Say a speck is merged into a neighbouring region that's itself small and not yet visited. When that region's flood fill runs later, it skips the speck's pixels (already `seen`). The region is then merged away, and the speck is left behind as a new isolated island of the region's old label. Higher Noise values merge more regions, so they leave more of these islands. On noisy images the path count therefore *rose* with Noise. On one test image it went 70 → 126 → 206 paths from Noise 50 to 100 to 200.

`denoise` now repeats its pass until a pass changes nothing. Every merge joins two components, so the loop always ends, with a 64-pass cap as a backstop. Real images settle in a few passes. While there, I made it return early when `labels` is shorter than `w × h` rather than index past the end.

## How it was tested

New tests in `crates/trace/src/tests.rs`. All three fail without the fix and pass with it:
- `denoise_leaves_no_island_behind_a_merged_region`: the minimal case, one row `[0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2]` with a minimum of 3. Before: `[1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2]` (the stranded island). After: all `2`.

title: Graph Type: widths past 100%, First Row and First Column in Front, Draw Filled Lines
author: IHAGI-c
body:
Merge #1119 first: this branch is on top of it (and #1115, #1092), all changing `generate()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/graph.rs`.

As [Format column, bar, and line graphs](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/automate-visualize-data/visualize-data/format-columns-bars-and-lines.html) describes:

**Column, Bar and Cluster Width from 1% to 1000%.**
- `clusterWidth` took at most 100 and drawing capped both widths at 100%. Both now take 1–1000 and are drawn as set, so past 100% the columns or clusters overlap.
- A graph of stacked columns only keeps its width formula up to 100%.
- The legend moves past columns that reach beyond the plot.

**First Row in Front / First Column in Front.**
- `firstColumnInFront` draws the first series over the others in its layer.
- `firstRowInFront` draws each series' first category over the next.
- Across series the series order decides. That way each series stays one group for Group Selection; giving the first category priority over every series would break that, so the parity doc notes the limit.

**Draw Filled Lines.**
- `filledLines` draws the connecting lines of line, scatter and radar graphs as 3 pt bands. Each band is filled with the series colour, whether that colour was set as a fill or, on a thin line, as a stroke, and has a thin black outline.
- A run whose points are all in one place, or a graph past 20,000 data points, keeps thin lines, since the band outlines are rebuilt on every change.

The Graph Type query lists the overlap options only for graphs with columns or bars, and Filled Lines only for graphs with lines, so the generic dialog doesn't offer options that do nothing.

**Our own choices**, where the page doesn't say: both overlap options start off, which is today's order, and the band is 3 pt wide.

**File format.** New fields (`firstRowInFront`, `firstColumnInFront`, `filledLines`) are written only when set.

title: Graphs keep their label formatting when drawn again
author: IHAGI-c
body:
Merge #1136 first: this branch is on top of it.

[Format the text in graphs](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/automate-visualize-data/visualize-data/format-the-text-in-graphs.html) formats a graph's text with the Character and Appearance controls, for the whole graph with the Selection tool or for picked labels with Group Selection. Until now that formatting was lost as soon as the graph was drawn again from its data, for example after Graph Data or Graph Type.

**What's kept.** A graph now keeps a character style for each kind of label:
- value axis numbers;
- category labels (the category axis, radar spokes, pie names);
- legend labels (beside the graph or across the top, or in wedges).

**How it's kept.**
- `text.setStyle`, `text.setFormat` and fill/stroke changes on a graph's labels apply the same change to their kind's kept style. Only what the user changed is kept, so a size given to the whole graph doesn't also freeze one label's colour, and every label of that kind follows. The change is applied as given, not in a scaled label's own units.
- A change to part of a label's text isn't kept.
- Labels are told apart by where the graph draws them, not by their text. Values come before the categories in the Axes group, every label of a scatter graph is a value, and every label of a radar graph is a category. So a category named "2" and the value axis' 2 stay apart.

**Layout follows the kept size.** Legend rows and the offsets from the axes and wedges follow a kept size, so bigger labels don't overlap. At 9 pt everything is placed exactly as before.

**Wedge labels.** They stay white on dark wedges unless the legend labels were given a colour of their own.

**Limits.** A kept style from a file is held to the Character controls' limits, since it is copied onto every label: sizes, leading, tracking, scales, stroke width and font name lengths.

title: Graph Data: a worksheet window
author: IHAGI-c
body:
Merge #1137 first: this branch is on top of it.

Object › Graph › Data, and the graph tool after drawing, now open the Graph Data window as a worksheet in place of a free-text CSV field, as [Add graph data](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/automate-visualize-data/visualize-data/add-graph-data.html) and [Adjust column width and decimal digits](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/automate-visualize-data/visualize-data/adjust-column-width.html) describe.

**The sheet.** The first row holds the series labels, the first column the category labels, and the other cells the values.

**Editing.** A click picks a cell, which is edited in the entry box above the sheet.
- Tab enters the cell and moves right, Enter (Return) moves down, and Shift with either goes the other way. The arrow keys move between cells.
- The entry box keeps the keys: egui doesn't move the focus on with Tab, and Enter in the box moves down rather than applying.
- Pasting tab- or line-separated text, such as a spreadsheet's cells, fills the cells from the picked one.

**Buttons.**
- **Import Data** reads a tab-separated text file: UTF-8, or UTF-16 with a byte-order mark as spreadsheets' "Unicode Text" export writes it. It reads at most a graph's 10,000 × 256 cells, each up to 256 characters.
- **Transpose row/column** and **Switch x/y** (scatter graphs) rearrange the sheet. Switch x/y does what `graph.setData {switchXY}` does. Transpose is off when it would make more series than a graph can hold.

title: Fix #1140: gradient stops blend colour and opacity apart on the canvas, as the exports do
author: Biromedic
body:
## What and why

Fixes #1140.

The canvas built its `peniko::Gradient`s with peniko's default, `InterpolationAlphaSpace::Premultiplied`. The rest of VectorCraft blends colour and opacity separately: `Gradient::sample` (which `expanded_stops` also uses for the midpoint stops), the PDF export (a colour shading plus an `/SMask`) and SVG viewers. With a transparent white stop into black, the canvas drew grey 127 halfway, where the PDF and the SVG show 191.

The fix is one call in `crates/render/src/paint.rs`: `.with_interpolation_alpha_space(peniko::InterpolationAlphaSpace::Unpremultiplied)`, which vello_common 0.2 supports. It covers linear, radial and focal gradients on fills, strokes and text, since they all go through `set_paint`. Opaque gradients look exactly as before: the two spaces only differ when stop opacities differ.

## How it was tested

- **New test** `crates/render/tests/gradient_alpha.rs`: every 7th pixel of linear and radial gradients with transparent stops (including an off-centre midpoint) must match `Gradient::sample` composited over white, within 4 levels.
  - On main it fails: `Linear (3,3) t=0.035: got [247, 247, 247], want [255, 255, 255]`.
  - With the fix it passes.
- **Checks that pass on Windows (MSVC, Rust 1.99):**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
  - `cargo clippy -p vectorcraft-render -p vectorcraft-svg --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: Fix #1141: SVG import keeps a mask whose art is all hidden, so its object stays hidden
author: Biromedic
body:
## What and why

Fixes #1141.

When every element inside an SVG `<mask>` is `visibility="hidden"`, `Importer::path` skips them all. `opacity_mask` is then left with no children, and its `0 => return None` dropped the mask, so the masked object was drawn whole. Chrome and resvg draw nothing there: hidden art leaves the mask black all over.

The fix removes that arm, so the mask is kept with empty art. The renderer's `mask_value` already turns empty art into black (clip) or white (no clip), inverted when the mask is, so all four option combinations come out right. The object also stays in the document, where it can be edited. The PDF export (backdrop, then art) and the SVG export handle empty mask art as they are.

## How it was tested

- **New test** `a_mask_whose_art_is_all_hidden_hides_its_object` in `crates/svg/tests/mask_options.rs`. For a hidden `<rect>` and for a `<g visibility="hidden">`, it checks that:
  - the square keeps its mask;
  - the mask art is empty;
  - the canvas is white where resvg draws the same file white.

title: #788: file.place frames an SVG by its viewBox when crop is given
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #788.

`file.place` of an SVG fitted and centred it by its art's bounds whatever `crop` said, so art drawn on a shared canvas lost its relative place and scale, and `crop: "crop"` and `crop: "bounding"` gave the same result without a word.

- **`crop: "crop"` given:** the SVG is framed and clipped by its viewBox (its artboard, as File › Open has it), as a PDF is by its page. `rect` and `at` fit and centre that frame, and `file.place.info` reports its size. The issue's repro now puts the path at (140, 160), 80 × 100, as the same art placed from a PDF does.
- **By default** (as Illustrator places an SVG, with no frame) **and with `"bounding"`:** still the art's bounds.
- `file.place`'s params doc and `docs/mcp.md` say which box `rect` and `at` fit.

**Test:** `an_svg_placed_with_crop_is_framed_by_its_viewbox` covers the issue's SVG with `crop: "crop"` (viewBox frame, clipped), with no crop, and with `"bounding"` (ink bounds). Full `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Part of #812: Ctrl/Cmd and Alt shape a star while it's dragged
author: bflatastic
body:
Part of #812 (the star ratio, raised by @x-daniel-17).

A star's inner radius was always half its outer one while drawing, so its ratio couldn't be changed. As Illustrator documents for the Star tool:

- **Ctrl/Cmd** during the drag keeps the inner radius where it is while the outer one follows the pointer. The new ratio stays once the key is let go, for the rest of the drag and for the next stars (`starRatio`).
- **Alt** keeps the star's shoulders straight: each point's sides line up with the next points', a ratio of cos(2π/n)/cos(π/n) (0.382 for five points). Stars with fewer than five points can't line up and keep their ratio.

Shift (rotation), ↑/↓ (points) and Space (move) work as before.

**Test:** `a_star_drag_holds_its_inner_radius_with_ctrl_and_straightens_with_alt` drags with Ctrl (inner radius stays 20 as the outer grows to 80), lets go (the ratio stays ¼), then holds Alt (0.382). Full `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: PDF export: warn when raster effects render below the requested resolution
author: KnottyDyes
body:
PDF export renders raster effects at the document's Raster Effects resolution, but a 64-million-pixel cap on each generated image can lower that resolution for large objects without any warning. Asking for 300 ppi can silently produce much less.

- When the cap lowers a raster effect's resolution, PDF export now returns a warning through the existing export-warning channel, naming the original object and giving the requested and achieved ppi.
- Pieces generated for one object are reported once, at the lowest achieved resolution.
- Exports where nothing is capped stay warning-free; the rendering and the cap itself are unchanged.
- The parity docs record the new warning.

Validation: the new cap test fails before the change; afterwards a capped export reports 2400 ppi requested and 1268.7 achieved. `cargo test -p vectorcraft-engine` (1,848 passed), clippy and fmt are clean, and `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: #1018: Edit Toolbar opens a drawer beside the toolbar; tools drag in and out
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1018.

Edit Toolbar (the ••• at the bottom of the Tools panel) showed All Tools as a centred popup. As Illustrator's Edit Toolbar works, it now opens a **drawer beside the toolbar**, by the ••• button:

- **Dimmed tools:** tools already in the toolbar are dimmed in the drawer; the active tool stays readable.
- **Drag and drop:** drag a tool from the drawer onto the toolbar to add it (between buttons gives it its own slot, onto a button adds it to that button's group), or drag a toolbar button into the drawer to remove it. Dragging within the toolbar moves a tool. A line or outline shows where it will land, and the tool's icon follows the pointer. The toolbar is only editable while the drawer is open, and flyouts don't open meanwhile.
- **Closing:** Escape, a click outside, or ••• again. Picking a tool in the drawer selects it, as before.
- **Saved edits:** Basic and Advanced keep their own edits, saved with the preferences (old preferences load; a hand-edited file is cleaned up; an edit back to the default clears them). A Reset button restores the default.
- **Commands** for MCP and the control channel: `window.editToolbar {open?}`, `toolbar.addTool {tool, slot?, place?: before|after|group}`, `toolbar.removeTool {tool, group?}`, `toolbar.reset`.

The drawer is its own module (`edit_toolbar.rs`); the old `allTools` dialog is gone. Three new labels are translated in the complete catalogs.

**Tests:** seven new tests, four of them headless frame tests with pointer and key events: placement by the ••• button, closing and picking; dimming; drag and drop in every direction, including that a dimmed tool doesn't drag and the toolbar is locked with the drawer closed; plus commands, persistence, drop zones and every tool listed once. title: Render: a shape far beyond any page is left undrawn, never crashing the app
author: bflatastic
body:
The import fuzzer (`engine/tests/import_fuzz.rs`) crashed now and then with `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN`. The cause: a shape whose coordinates or stroke width are absurdly large on screen (say 1e15 pt) makes vello_cpu 0.2 either panic in `flatten_simd` or try to allocate tens of gigabytes. Both abort the process: rayon aborts on a worker panic, and a failed allocation can't be caught. So a malformed file could crash the app and lose unsaved work.

`draw_shape` now skips a shape whose device-space bounds or stroke width are not finite or exceed 1e10 px. Such a shape is far beyond any page, so nothing visible is lost.

## Verification
- New test `shapes_far_beyond_the_page_are_left_undrawn_without_crashing` (`crates/render/tests/stroke_geometry.rs`). Without the guard it aborts with a 132 GB allocation.
- `vectorcraft-cli perf`: render times are unchanged within noise. Two alternating runs each on an idle machine, against main: fit page 72.3 / 72.5 vs 71.6 / 71.7 ms, pan refresh 72.1 / 71.2 vs 71.5 / 71.8 ms, 400% zoom 23.4 / 23.3 vs 23.4 / 23.4 ms. The 400% zoom budget is already over on main.

title: Reject malformed desktop automation root arguments before startup
author: piero-83
body:
## What and why

A desktop invocation such as `vectorcraft --control 7979 --automation-read-root` silently replaces the read root with `None`. If no write root is set, it starts the control channel without confinement, including when an environment variable had supplied a read root. Root argument parsing also accepts empty or repeated flags and can consume the next option as a folder.

Validate both root flags before logging, font discovery, preferences or window initialization. Missing or empty values, another option in place of a value, and repeated flags now produce a specific error and exit. A valid command-line root overrides its environment default once; folders beginning with `-` remain accepted through `--flag=-folder` or `./-folder`.

Add desktop startup regressions and expand the CLI MCP test to cover traversal, symlink and dangling-link escape attempts, preservation of an outside file, and a successful request after rejected requests. This builds on the confinement engine already merged in #919; it does not replace that work.

## How it was tested

`cargo xtask ci` passed all seven gates on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.99.0: fmt, strict Clippy, workspace tests, assets, brands, layers and WASM checks (21 crates). The test run had 5,296 passes, no failures and four ignored tests. `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` was unset.

The regressions cover parser preservation of environment defaults; desktop processes exiting promptly with the exact error before initialization; duplicate flags; explicit dash-prefixed folders; and MCP traversal/symlink rejection, outside-file preservation and recovery after a rejected request. `git diff --check` also passed.

title: #1144: Live Corners round corners between curved segments too
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1144.

Live Corners only rounded an anchor where two straight sides meet. As in Illustrator, any corner can now be rounded, including one where a curve meets a line or two curves meet.

- **Which anchors count as corners:** any anchor that isn't smooth, where the two sides meet at an angle. The angle is measured between the directions the sides leave the anchor.
- **Where the cut goes:** it meets each side at its setback, measured *along* the curve. Its handles follow each side's direction at those points, so the result stays smooth. Each curved side is trimmed to the part the cuts at its ends leave, and it keeps its shape.
- **Largest radius:** still the one that takes the cut halfway along the shorter side, with lengths measured along curves.
- **Unchanged:**
  - Corners between straight sides draw exactly as before, and their existing tests pass as they were.
  - The widgets, the Corners dialog, `object.setLiveShape` and the Properties/Transform fields work on curved corners through the same code.
- **Text updated:** the Corners dialog's error message (with its translations), the command docs and `docs/mcp.md` no longer say "two straight sides".

## Verification
- New test `corners_next_to_curves_are_cut_along_them`:
  - the cut ends lie on the original curve;
  - the trimmed curve still follows it;
  - every anchor's handles are in line (smooth).
- Updated the tests that asserted curved corners are skipped.
- Checked in the running app over the control channel:
  - a square with one bulging side rounds at all four corners;
  - a lens made of two curves chamfers where they meet;
  - a D shape takes inverted-round corners;
  - Direct Selection shows the widgets on the curved corners.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes. The first run failed only in `tests_place::a_file_placed_while_idle_follows_its_changes`, a file-watch timing test, while the machine was busy; it passed on the re-run.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across VectorCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for VectorCraft.

title: Type: Thai falls back to a font made for Thai
author: bflatastic

Characters of Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar now try fonts made for their script first. Installed ones are loaded on demand, then the fallback carries on as before:

- **Lao, Khmer and Myanmar:** their Windows, macOS and Noto fonts.

Latin beside them keeps the font chosen. The app's own interface uses the same fallback (`face_covering`), so Thai in layer names and fields gets the same font.

title: Type: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar lines break between words
author: bflatastic
body:
Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar don't separate words with spaces. Lines broke only at spaces, hyphens and CJK characters, so a Thai paragraph in area type ran on to the next space, or was cut wherever it overflowed.

- **Word ends:** each paragraph's shaped glyphs now carry the word ends that ICU4X's line segmenter (`icu_segmenter`, Unicode-3.0, the same family as the `icu_properties` already in the build) finds in text of those scripts. A line may break after them, as after a space. The every-line and single-line composers both use them, since they go through `break_after`.
- **Data:** the desktop uses ICU's dictionaries, the most accurate; they keep loanwords such as โปรแกรม whole, which the LSTM model split in a live test. The web build uses the far smaller LSTM models, to keep its size down.
- **Unchanged:**
  - Latin, CJK and other text keep their own breaks, and nothing is segmented when a paragraph has none of those scripts.

author: alpha-rock
body:
## What and why

Follow-up to #846 and the next steps discussed in #605. Flat Revolve shading shows bands on curved profiles, and open profiles cannot currently close their circular ends.

title: Linux: Automatic draws on the GPU the Wayland compositor draws with
author: atoslins
body:
**Problem.** On a hybrid laptop whose Wayland compositor runs on the discrete GPU, VectorCraft 0.9.0 opens an empty window under Automatic: nothing drawn, no error. The built-in panel hangs off the integrated GPU, so the display rule puts it ahead of the system's order:

```
vectorcraft::gpu: graphics adapters: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 6GB Laptop GPU (Vulkan, DiscreteGpu, Vulkan:10de:25ac); Intel(R) Graphics (RPL-P) (Vulkan, IntegratedGpu, Vulkan:8086:a7a8, drives the primary display); NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 6GB Laptop GPU/PCIe/SSE2 (Gl, Other, Gl:10de:0000, can't show the window)
vectorcraft::gpu: drawing on Intel(R) Graphics (RPL-P) (Vulkan, IntegratedGpu): it drives the primary display
```

The compositor takes those frames and shows nothing. Nothing fails, so the restart doesn't trigger (#502, #519). The UI keeps running frames, so the first-frame watch (#964) doesn't trigger either. `WGPU_POWER_PREF=high` works around it. Mesa's device-select layer had already put the right GPU first in the system's order; the panel rule overrode it.

Machine: Intel Raptor Lake-P iGPU (`8086:a7a8`, drives the eDP panel) + RTX 3050 Laptop (`10de:25ac`), Arch Linux, kernel 7.2, Mesa 26.2.2, NVIDIA 610.57.04, Hyprland 0.56.2 with `AQ_DRM_DEVICES=<nvidia>:<intel>`. That setting makes the NVIDIA GPU the compositor's primary; it is needed to drive a 240 Hz HDMI monitor wired to the NVIDIA GPU without a cross-GPU copy per frame.

**Change.** Which GPU drives a display stands in for which GPU the compositor draws with. Under Wayland the compositor says so itself: the `main_device` of its linux-dmabuf feedback (protocol version 4), the device it imports client buffers on. Mesa's device-select layer reads the same event for the same purpose (`default_dmabuf_feedback_main_device` in `src/vulkan/device-select-layer/device_select_wayland.c`).

- `compositor_gpu.rs` asks for it on a short-lived connection of its own, before the window opens. It maps the `dev_t` to PCI ids through `/sys/dev/c…

title: Part of #1102: type from the text document keeps its line spacing across paragraphs
author: DisasterAreaDesigns
body:
Part of #1102 (the tight three-line label). The page-size and stroke problems of that issue were fixed in #1120.

## The bug

`Story::node` (`crates/eps/src/import/ate.rs`) takes the leading of a text object made from the file's text document from the distance between the first two lines of the file's own layout. Those lines are already where the paragraph spacing has put them, and the text object applies the paragraph spacing again.

The case in the issue: a 13 pt label of three paragraphs, each with a space after of -5 pt. The layout's lines are 10.6 pt apart (auto leading 15.6 pt less 5 pt). The text object got `leading` 10.6 and then the -5 pt again, so its lines were 5.6 pt apart and overlapped. A positive space after has the same fault the other way: lines too far apart.

## The fix

The leading is the distance less the space after the paragraph before and the space before the paragraph after (`Story::line_leading`). Two lines of one paragraph (a line break) have no paragraph spacing between them, so their distance is used as before. The frame's scale is applied as before.

## Checked

- On the file from the issue (my own, kept local): the three lines come out 10.6 pt apart in the app and in the SVG export, as in a Ghostscript render. Before it was 5.6 pt.
- `vectorcraft-eps`: 160 tests pass, including two new ones on synthetic stories made of plain numbers (negative and positive spacing, a frame scale, a line break inside a paragraph, a single line). `vectorcraft-engine`: the EPS tests pass.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p vectorcraft-eps --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets|brands|layers` are clean.
- Not run here: the full `cargo xtask ci` (the whole workspace's tests and the wasm check).
- No docs changed: this is a fix inside the text import, with no new row or number in the parity docs.

No test input is derived from a file made with another vendor's app; the tests construct the story's numbers directly.

title: .ai import: copied area type and type on a path keep their own place
author: p0lyg0n
body:
In a `.ai` read through its editing data, every copy of a piece of area type or type on a path landed on top of its original.

The text document's frame for a copied object keeps the original's path. It carries a matrix of its own (`/2 [ 1 0 0 1 tx ty ]`), but I couldn't pin down how that matrix maps to the page: the x offsets match the copies' spacing, while adding the y offset puts the frames off the page, so I didn't guess at it. Each `/AI11Text` object in the layers' data already carries its own `/Art` path (before `/ConfiningPath`), in absolute art-space coordinates, written with the documented path operators.

- `ai/frames.rs`: `text_frames(data)` reads each text object's `/Art` path, keyed by story and frame (`/StoryIndex`, `/FrameIndex`), on plain lines or lines led by `%_`. It caps object count and size, and objects without a readable path are skipped.
- `native.rs`: when a story's frame is area type or type on a path, its node takes the object's own path as frame or path. Its region, which is used to match the page's type, is recomputed from that path. Point type is untouched, and so is any object without an `/Art` path.

Tests:
- `frames::each_text_object_has_its_own_frame_by_story_and_frame`.
- `tests_native::a_copied_area_type_object_is_framed_where_its_own_art_path_is`: the text document frames the story at its original; the copy's `/Art` frames it elsewhere, and the area type lands there. The test fails without the change.

On a real file of cards made by copying one card (two artboards, 515 text objects on its PDF part), opening it through the editing data gave 467 text objects, with every card's description and title arc piled onto one card. With this change all 515 come back, with the same text in the same place as the PDF part. The only remaining difference is the second artboard, which keeps the file's spacing.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: fix: 選択アンカーだけを整列する #1180
author: haranishi
body:
## What and why

Closes #1180.

Direct Selectionでパスの一部のアンカーを選んだとき、Alignがパス全体を移動する不具合を修正します。`M100 40 L200 60 L150 160 Z` の上側2点を選んでVertical Align Centerを実行すると、選択点のYが50に揃い、3点目は `(150, 160)` に残ります。

選択点の位置から整列範囲を求め、各アンカーとそのハンドルを移動します。Align to Artboardにも対応します。パスが1つでもアンカー選択中はAlignパネルの指定先を使います。変更は1回のUndoで戻り、同じ整列を繰り返してもUndo履歴を増やしません。

操作仕様は[公開ドキュメント](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/arrange-objects/align-and-distribute-objects.html)を参照しました。キーアンカーによる整列は引き続き未実装です。

## How it was tested

- エンジンの回帰テスト5件：選択点の上端・中央・下端整列、ハンドル追従、Undo/Redo、アートボードへの2軸整列、別パス間の整列、変化のない整列、パス全体の整列。
- eguiのポインターイベントでAlignパネルのVertical Align Centerをクリックし、選択点だけが動くことを検証。

title: #1197: Make Compound Path cuts holes where paths overlap
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1197.

Make Compound Path kept each path's direction under the non-zero fill rule. A shape drawn inside or across another, running the same way, so left the overlap filled instead of cutting a hole, which is what a compound path is used for.

The paths in front of the backmost one now run against it: each is reversed when its first subpath turns the same way as the backmost path's. So where they overlap it, they cut holes, and where they stick out, they stay filled.

## Verification
- New engine test `a_compound_path_has_holes_where_its_paths_overlap`, with a square and an overlapping larger diamond as in the reporter's video: a click in the overlap goes through, and the square's corner and the diamond's point outside it are filled.
- The existing compound path tests pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Test: the idle place test waits for the link scan in real time
author: bflatastic
body:
`tests_place::a_file_placed_while_idle_follows_its_changes` failed at random in CI, twice today. While the link scan ran on its worker thread, the test's simulated clock moved on by whole seconds for every 5 ms of real time. On a busy machine, the 10 simulated seconds ran out before the scan had read the changed file.

The clock now waits for a running scan in real time, up to 20 seconds. Test-only change.

## Verification
- The place tests pass three runs in a row locally.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: #1194: Direct3D 12 shaders compile with FXC
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1194.

wgpu's default DX12 shader compiler (`Auto`) loads whichever `dxcompiler.dll` the DLL search path finds first. VectorCraft ships none, so it was another program's. One without its `dxil.dll` warns that the DXIL is unsigned, and wgpu takes the warning for a compile error. The device is then lost before the first frame, and the app falls back to OpenGL.

The window's DX12 shaders now compile with FXC (`d3dcompiler_47.dll`, part of Windows), as LightCraft does since storytold/lightcraft#484. `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` still picks another compiler.

## Verification
- The release build starts and renders on Direct3D 12 here ("rendering with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (Dx12, DiscreteGpu)", no shader errors).
- Not reproduced: the reporter's broken `dxcompiler.dll` setup.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: #1180: Align aligns the selected anchor points
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #1180.

With anchor points selected by Direct Selection, the Align buttons moved the whole path, so two points couldn't be lined up. `object.align` operated on whole objects only. It now aligns the selected points themselves, as Illustrator does:
- **Align To Selection:** the points move to the edge or centre of their own bounds.
- **Align To Artboard:** they move to the artboard's edges or centre.
- **Paths selected whole** still align as objects.

Not included: Illustrator's Key Anchor option (aligning to one clicked anchor). VectorCraft has no key anchor yet, so with anchors selected, Align To Key Object behaves like Selection. It's noted in the code.

## Verification
- New engine test `align_moves_selected_anchor_points`, with the issue's triangle: two points to their top, then to the artboard's centre; the third point stays; a whole path keeps its shape. The existing align tests pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes. The first run failed only in the file-watch test fixed separately.

title: #955: a move grabbed by an anchor lands it on another anchor
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #955.

With Smart Guides on, a selection moved with the Selection tool only lined its bounds up with the other art. Grabbed by an anchor and dropped near another object's anchor, it could stop a fraction of a point beside it, where one of its edges lined up instead. In the reporter's GIF it was 0.25 pt off.

Now, when the grabbed point comes within the snapping tolerance of an anchor or a centre, it lands exactly there, as Smart Guides' anchor snapping does. Otherwise the bounds line up as before.

## Verification
- New tools test `a_move_grabbed_by_an_anchor_lands_it_on_another_anchor`: a rectangle grabbed by its corner and dropped next to a triangle's tip lands on (350.3, 250). Without the change it lands at (350, 250).
- All 300 tools tests pass.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Tests: the command sweeps and import fuzz tests fail when a command panics
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

`Session::execute` runs each top-level command inside the engine's guard, which turns a panic into

empty-params, junk-params and structured-junk sweeps call.

Each of these checks now passes the command's result through `no_panic`, which the tests of library files in
`import_fuzz.rs` have used since #644, and `command_sweep.rs` gets a copy of it. A case whose command panics now

title: Tests: the envelope export test ignores the PDF's XMP dates and file ID
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

`enveloped_type_exports_distorted_in_every_format` in `crates/engine/src/tests_envelope.rs` exports each format twice
and compares the two files without the lines that contain `CreationDate` or `ModDate` (#188). Two other lines of the
PDF also change with the time it was written. The XMP packet is one line that holds `xmp:CreateDate`,
`xmp:ModifyDate` and the file ID, and the trailer holds the file ID as `/ID`. The file ID is a hash that krilla
computes over the bytes written before it, which include the dates. When the two PDF exports are written in different
seconds, these two lines differ and the test fails at "pdf exports are repeatable". In a local `cargo xtask ci` run on
2026-10-10, the two exports were written at 22:37:23 UTC and 22:37:24 UTC, and the test failed this way.

The comparison now also drops the lines that contain `xmp:CreateDate`, `xmp:ModifyDate` or `/ID[`. A new check in the
test writes the PDF that `document.export` writes, with its creation time set to Unix seconds 0 and then 1, and
asserts that the comparison's filter leaves the two files equal. The pull request changes only `tests_envelope.rs`.
The other tests that compare two PDF exports byte for byte set the creation time to 0
(`crates/pdf/src/tests_webview.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests_brushsym.rs`).

## How it was tested

On macOS 27.0.1 (Apple Silicon) with rustc 1.99.0, on top of `main` at 4eaa5f0:

- With a 1.1 s pause between the two exports of each format, a copy of the test's export loop fails at "pdf exports

title: Align: Align to Key Object makes the topmost selected object the key
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

With two or more objects selected and no key object, a click on Align to Key Object in the Align panel stored Key as
the Align To choice and set no key. The align buttons of the Align panel, the Control bar and the Properties panel
then sent `to: "key"`, and the status bar showed "no key object". Distribute Spacing sent the panel's spacing value
and kept the leftmost or top object in place. The stored Key stayed until Align to Selection, Align to Artboard or
Cancel Key Object was chosen.

The button now runs `select.key` on the topmost selected object, the last in paint order, whatever order the objects
were selected in, and the canvas draws that object with the key-object outline. The align buttons in all three places
and Distribute Spacing then use that key, and Cancel Key Object clears it. A key that is already set stays the key.
With fewer than two objects selected the button is disabled, as the Distribute buttons are. The button stores no
choice, so once the key is cleared by Cancel Key Object, by a click on the key object or by another selection, Align To
shows the stored Selection or Artboard choice again. `object.align` with `to: "key"` and no key still returns "no key
object" to agents. `docs/target-app-parity.md` gets a line under Evidence › Tools › Selection.

Adobe's help pages describe setting a key by clicking a selected object again and do not say what the button does
without a key. On Adobe's feedback site, Egor Chistyakov (Admin, Adobe Illustrator) wrote on 2022-01-05 that "the
topmost object is used by default when you change the option to Align to Key Object in Align panel", and wrote on

title: MCP: select.key checks its id, and agents can read the key object
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

Agents could set and clear the key object but not read it: `document.inspect`, the control channel's `ui.pointer`
reply and the headless `pointer_gesture` reply left it out, and `select.key` returned null. `select.key` with an id
that was not selected, or with a value that is not an id, such as `"x"`, cleared the key without an error. A
compound-path member or an object inside a selected group could become the key.

- `select.key` checks its id with `checked_id`, as `select.set`, `select.add` and `select.toggle` do (#784). It
  returns an error for an id that is not a selected top-level object and leaves the key as it was. Layers,
  compound-path members and objects inside another selected object are not top-level objects. The check runs
  `roots_of` (`cmd/edit.rs`, which `selected_roots` uses) over the selected objects among the id and its ancestors.
  Without `id`, `select.key` clears the key as before. `select.key {id: null}` used to clear it too, and it is now
  an error.
- `select.key` returns `{key}`. `document.inspect` reports the key object as `key`, and the `ui.pointer` and
  `pointer_gesture` replies list it beside `selection`.
- In isolation mode a Selection-tool click can pick an object that `select.key` does not accept as the key: a
  sublayer inside an isolated layer, a member inside an isolated compound path, or an object in an isolated group
  that is also selected (through the Layers panel's selection column, for example). The tool no longer sends
  `select.key {id}` for such an object. When the object is already the key, the tool still sends `select.key {}`,
  which clears the key.
- A recorded action whose `select.key` step names an object that is not a selected top-level object when the action
  plays now fails and is rolled back, as an action with a `select.set` step naming a deleted object has failed since
  #784.

## How it was tested

- `select_key_rejects_ids_it_cannot_use_and_keeps_the_key` and `select_key_and_do…
