title: Shape Builder: a line's loose end past a crossing no longer runs out and back in most cases
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

Since #1035 moved linesweeper to 0.5, the sweep can cut the paths through one crossing at points more than its
tolerance (`eps`) apart. `map` in `crates/pathops/src/planar.rs` merges a point only into a vertex within `eps` of it,
so the two passes of an open path can end on two different vertices, and on `main` the map keeps them as two edges with
different ends. On `main` at 4eaa5f0, take the line from (30,20) to (70,0), the line from (40,0) to (0,90) and the
square from (10,0) to (40,30):

- `shape_builder` returns the first line's loose end as one piece that runs from the crossing out to (30,20) and back.
  It also returns an extra piece of the second line, 1.4e-6 long.
- In `live_paint`, the face left of the second line runs out along the loose end and back.
- `FaceMerger::merge` of all the faces, which the Shape Builder uses to merge regions, returns the square and a second
  subpath from the crossing to (30,20).

This is a minimal failing input of `pieces_cut_out_of_their_inputs` (the case proptest saved), which fails on `main`:
`cut_out` treats the loose end, whose ends are 1.4e-6 apart, as running all the way around and removes the whole line.

`map` now joins the ends of pieces whose middles and ends lie within `16 * eps` of each other. The two passes then
share their ends and become one edge.

bflatastic [noted on #1081](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/1081#issuecomment-6105822529) that a
property test had found a planar-cutting case ("an open line starting on a closed square's corner loses its piece")
and that it is tracked as a follow-up. The input above has a line that starts on the square's corner (40,0). The
comment gives no input, so this change was not checked against that case.

## How it was tested

`a_loose_end_is_one_piece_when_the_sweep_cuts_its_passes_apart` in `crates/pathops/src/planar.rs` builds that input. It
checks that each path comes back in three pieces, that cutting each piece out of its path removes onl…

title: Object: Lock, Transform Each, Perspective and other commands that change nothing record no undo step
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

These commands edited the document even when nothing changed, so the call recorded an undo step, emptied Redo and
marked the document modified, as the commands in `object.rs` did before #1060:

- All Artwork Above and Other Layers (Object › Lock and Object › Hide) with nothing to lock or hide: no object above
  the selection, no other layer, or every one already locked (Lock) or hidden (Hide).
- Transform Each with no object to transform, and without Copy when both scales are 100% and there is no move,
  rotation or reflection.
- Rearrange All Artboards when no artboard moves, or with no artboard.
- `stroke.widthPoint.set` and `stroke.widthPoint.copy` when the profile comes out as it was, and
  `stroke.widthProfile.set` with the profile the strokes have already.
- Liquify when the stroke reshapes no path, and Puppet Warp given the pins the art holds already (`rest: true`), or
  without `rest` when every pin stays where it is and turns the art by 0° or is free.
- Define Perspective Grid with the grid the document has, Attach to Active Plane with no object, Release with
  Perspective on art that is not in perspective, Move Plane to where the plane is (without copies), and Move Plane to
  Match Object when the plane is there and active already.
- Move, Nudge and Transform in Perspective without Copy when no object moves (1e-9 pt or less along the plane or its

title: Direct Selection: a click on an already selected anchor selects it alone
author: zakariayacine
body:
## What and why

With the Direct Selection tool, clicking an anchor of a path that is selected whole (or of a set of selected anchors)
left the selection as it was: every anchor stayed selected and the clicked one never showed as the selected anchor.
In practice, after selecting a shape with the Selection tool and switching to Direct Selection (the common way to
reach a corner), a click on a corner's anchor couldn't narrow the selection to that corner, so Live Corners and the
anchor controls kept acting on every corner.

A plain click selects the anchor alone, as the public documentation describes (click selects the anchor point,
Shift-click adds others): https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/select-anchor-points-in-paths.html

The press still keeps the selection, so a drag moves every selected anchor with the one held, as before; only the
release without a drag narrows it. Shift still toggles, Alt still picks the whole path, and pressing an anchor that
wasn't selected still selects it on the press.

Reproduced on the running app through the control channel: `shape.rectangle`, `object.setLiveShape {radius: 20}`,
`select.set`, Direct Selection, `ui.pointer` down/up on an arc anchor → the selection stayed the whole path and all
eight anchors drew alike; with the fix the clicked anchor is the selection and draws in the selected-anchor colour.

## How it was tested

- `direct::tests::a_click_on_a_selected_anchor_selects_it_alone`: a click on an anchor of a path selected whole, and
  of a two-anchor selection, returns `select.anchors {mode: "set"}` for that anchor on the release; a drag instead
  moves and commits with the selection kept; an unselected anchor is selected on the press and the release adds nothing.
- The existing `pressing_an_anchor_of_a_fully_selected_path_keeps_the_selection` (drag) and the other Direct
  Selection tests pass unchanged.

title: Hand and Zoom cursors drawn like the tool cursors (Windows showed the move arrows, no magnifier)
author: zakariayacine
body:
## What and why

On Windows the Hand tool, Space and the Zoom tool showed the wrong cursors: winit maps egui's `Grab` and
`Grabbing` to the four-headed move cursor (`IDC_SIZEALL`, `winit/src/platform_impl/windows/util.rs`) and has
nothing for `ZoomIn`/`ZoomOut`, so holding Space showed arrows instead of a hand, and the Zoom tool (Z) showed no
magnifier. Those four were the only tool cursors left to the system (`cursors.rs` drew every other tool).

They are now vector glyphs like the others, in the same visual grammar (black on a white halo, Illustrator's
grammar): an open hand with the thumb to the left (Hand tool, Space), the same hand closed while the view is
dragged, and a magnifier with a plus in the lens or a minus with Alt. Shown as OS cursors on the desktop (#444) and
painted on the web as the other glyphs are. The canvas routes the Space, Hand and Zoom states through the same path
as the tool cursors instead of asking egui for system cursors.

## How it was tested

- `cursors::tests`: the four glyphs rasterize at every scale with the other 34, inside the 50 px limit, with an
  opaque body and the hotspot inside the bitmap; only the busy state (`NotAllowed`) stays a system cursor.

- Seen on Windows 11 in a release build: Space shows the hand, dragging the closed hand, Z the magnifier, Alt the

title: Live Corners: with Direct Selection, a click on a widget selects its corner
author: zakariayacine
body:
## What and why

Reworked after review. The first version made a Direct Selection drag on a whole-path selection round one corner; the
documented workflow is to select the corner first, then drag its widget, so a drag keeps rounding every shown corner
as before.

What was missing is the first half of that workflow on the widget itself: with Direct Selection, a plain **click** on a
corner widget (press and release, no drag) now selects that corner, exactly as a click on the corner's anchor does
(#1237), and Shift-click toggles it. The widget is then the only one showing and the next drag on it rounds that
corner alone. Selecting a corner by its round, then dragging it, is how long-time users remember rounding a single
corner.

Unchanged: a drag on a whole-path selection rounds every corner with both tools, Alt-click still cycles the corner
kind, the Selection tool's click on a widget still does nothing, and corners picked by their anchors edit together.

title: perf: bound memory on large documents (#1244)
author: arhammusheer
body:
Large documents held far more memory than their content needs, and some of it grew without limit during a session (#1244). This PR bounds it and makes open and save stream. Output is identical: the `perf --deep` SVG export and save → open → save hashes match `main`, and saved JSON is byte-identical.

## Results

`vectorcraft-cli perf --paths 50000 --deep` on an Apple M2 Pro, `main` vs this branch, run back to back:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Peak memory footprint | 2,982 MB | **1,480 MB** (−50 %) |
| Peak RSS | 3,709 MB | **2,566 MB** (−31 %) |
| Open `.vectorcraft`, 50k paths | 202 ms | **126 ms** |
| Save `.vectorcraft`, 50k paths | 58 ms | **47 ms** |
| 4 embedded 24 MP photos drawn by 3 renderers | 2,015 ms | **685 ms** |
| Undo / redo of a 50k-path move | 5.9 / 6.0 ms | 6.5 / 6.1 ms |
| Render fit page / after a pan / 400 %, nudge | — | unchanged |

Opening and saving a big file, release CLI (`/usr/bin/time -l`):

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Open, 50k-path file (gzip) | 444 MB, 0.34 s | **154 MB**, 0.24 s |
| Open and save, 50k-path file (gzip) | 493 MB, 0.85 s | **155 MB**, 0.75 s |
| Open and save, 4 JPEGs + 1 PNG (gzip) | 183 MB, 0.73 s | **80 MB**, 0.12 s |

Data Recovery for the photo document writes about 35.5 MB every interval on `main`. Here it writes the images once, then about 32 KB per interval.

## Changes, one commit each

1. **Decoded images** live once in a process-wide LRU store with a byte budget, instead of a full-resolution copy in every renderer that is never evicted. Mip levels are opt-in (`RenderOptions::image_mips`): on for the canvas and thumbnails, off for exports. Thumbnail renders sweep their caches. Shadow and effect rasters have a byte budget and match their node by `Arc`.
2. **Undo history** is bounded by bytes (1 GiB, or ⅛ of RAM where known) as well as steps, and always keeps the last 8. Documents entering history drop their id index. Selections are shared between steps. The command journal is bounded,…

title: MCP: lost replies report uncertainty instead of replaying edits
author: KnottyDyes
body:
When a request to the running app fails mid-flight, the MCP remote backend reconnects and sends the same request again. A lost reply doesn't mean the request wasn't applied, so an edit can be applied twice.

- A failed request now drops the connection and returns an error saying the operation may have completed and the document should be inspected before retrying. It is never resent.
- The next request reconnects as before, so a restarted app is still picked up. This matches how PhotoCraft's bridge behaves.

Validation: a loopback test server applies a real rectangle through the headless engine and closes the connection before replying. Before the change the rectangle was drawn twice; now it is drawn once, the call returns an error and the next call reconnects and inspects the document. `cargo test -p vectorcraft-mcp` (85 passed) and `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, brands, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Trace: colour mode keeps close dark tones apart
author: japbcoelho
body:
## What and why

Colour Image Trace binned colours by the top 5 bits of each channel (`r >> 3`), so tones less than 8 values apart always shared a bin and could never get their own palette entry, however many colours were asked for. A dark, low-contrast photo (a book-cover texture with RGB 33..66) traced to 5 colours when 12 were requested, and eight grey stripes 32..39 traced to one:

```
vectorcraft-cli run --in stripes-32-39.png --cmd select.all --cmd imageTrace.makeAndExpand \
  --params '{"params":{"mode":"color","colors":8,"noise":0,"method":"overlapping"}}'
-> {"anchors":4,"colors":1,"id":4,"paths":1}
```

The histogram keeps its 32×32×32 bins, now fitted to each channel's range among the opaque pixels (`HistKey`): a channel spanning at most 32 values keeps every value apart, a full-range channel keeps the old 5-bit bins. Logo mode, which quantises like Color when asked directly, gets the same.

## How it was tested

New tests in `crates/trace/src/tests.rs`: `color_mode_separates_close_dark_tones` (the eight stripes give eight colours) and `color_mode_full_range_and_transparent_inputs`. The stripes case reproduces with the v0.9.0 release CLI (1 colour) and gives 8 colours with the fix. On main `d1a6926f`: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p vectorcraft-trace --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p vectorcraft-trace` pass.

title: SVG: physicalSize writes width and height in points
author: japbcoelho
body:
## What and why

This is the opt-in option proposed in #1093 and #864: SVG export writes the artboard size as unitless `width`/`height` (one pixel per point, as now by default), and other SVG readers take unitless lengths as CSS pixels at 96 per inch. A 948.83 × 613.28 pt book-cover background opened in Inkscape, browsers and rsvg at 75 % of its printed size (251 mm instead of 334.7 mm wide).

The new SVG option `physicalSize` (default false, so the default output doesn't change; ignored with `responsive`) writes `width="948.83pt" height="613.28pt"`. The viewBox stays in points, and VectorCraft reads the file back at the same size. It is one of `document.export`'s SVG options (flat or inside `svg: {...}`) and listed with them; there is no checkbox in the SVG Options dialog yet. Before this change, the option was ignored at the top level of `document.export` and rejected inside `svg: {...}` as an unknown field.

## How it was tested

New tests: `crates/svg/tests/physical_size.rs`, `physical_size_writes_points_and_reads_back_the_same`; and a `physicalSize` case in `every_option_changes_the_output` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_svg.rs`). With the v0.9.0 release CLI a 72 × 36 pt artboard exports `width="72" height="36"` whatever the options; with the change and `physicalSize: true` it is `width="72pt" height="36pt"`. On main `d1a6926f`: `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and the tests of `vectorcraft-svg` and `vectorcraft-engine` pass.

title: Color params: one scale per CMYK colour, not per component
author: japbcoelho
body:
## What and why

`paint.setFill {"color": {"c": 18.16, "m": 13.39, "y": 13.9, "k": 0.79}}` stored K 79 %: `recolor.colors` listed the colour as `cmyk 18.16 13.39 13.9 79` and the exported PDF printed a light grey as a dark one. `color_value` chose the scale for each component on its own (above 1: percent, else a fraction), so a percentage of 1 or less beside larger ones became a fraction.

A `{c, m, y, k}` object is now read on one scale: percent for every component as soon as one is above 1, fractions only when all four are within 0..1, as before. The doc comment says so. storytold/designcraft#510 makes the same change in DesignCraft.

## How it was tested

New test `cmyk_object_reads_one_scale_for_every_component` in `crates/engine/src/tests_recolor.rs`. The colour above reproduces with the v0.9.0 release CLI (`cmyk 18.16 13.39 13.9 79`) and is stored as `cmyk 18.16 13.39 13.9 0.79` with the fix. title: feat: 定規の原点を変更・リセットする #1212

## What and why

Closes #1212

定規の交点をドラッグすると、目盛りと十字線で位置をプレビューし、キャンバス上で離した点を新しい原点として設定します。交点のダブルクリックでは、表示中のアートボードの左上へ戻します。画面外へのドロップ、Escape、フォーカス喪失、文書切り替えでは変更を中止します。

author: haranishi
body:
## What and why

Closes #1253

線なしの図形をスポイトで参照すると、幅0が新しい図形へ引き継がれ、線の色を付けても見えませんでした。色を付ける時に、未着色かつ幅0の線を既存の既定幅1 ptへ戻します。塗りと線の交換、個別の外観項目、新しい図形の既定値にも適用します。

正の幅はそのまま使います。色がある線に明示的に設定した幅0も、色の変更では維持します。塗りの編集や線の色をNoneにする操作は幅を変更しません。図形と選択は変えず、色と幅の変更をUndo一回で戻せます。既定幅の基準は既存の `PaintDefaults::default` と `Appearance::set_stroke` の1 ptです。関連資料の点数と残り時間は維持しました。

title: i18n (cs): translate labels that bypass the catalog lookup (file filters, diagnostics, credits, gradients, print marks)
author: Losminek
body:
Follow-up to #1189 and #1226 (Czech catalog). The catalog is complete, but a few labels never reach the
catalog lookup, so they still show in English under Czech. This PR translates them where they are shown,
from a variable or a template, so every other language keeps its current behaviour and falls back to
English. No new `tl!("literal")` keys, so only `cs.tsv` gains rows.

## What changes

- **File dialog filters** (desktop `apps/vectorcraft/src/main.rs`, web `apps/vectorcraft-web/src/web.rs`):
  filter names such as "All readable files", "Swatch libraries", "PDF presets" are looked up when the
  dialog is built (context `file-filter`). Extensions and format names stay as they are.
- **Diagnostics line** (`chrome.rs`): the words `render` / `ui` are looked up (context `diagnostics`);
  numbers, `ms` and `fps` stay.
- **New Document**: the suggested name is the template `Preset {number}` instead of `format!("Preset {}")`.
- **Credits**: the `PRs` column header and the contributor tooltip go through named placeholders, with
  `@plural` rows for PR and commit counts. Names and handles stay unchanged.
- **Gradients**: Czech needs the adjective before the noun and in agreement, so `{kind} Gradient` now reads
  "Lineární přechod" / "Kruhový přechod"; `Radial` got a `gradient-kind` context for the masculine form.
- **"Japanese" collision**: the English key is both the language name and a printer mark style in PDF/Print.

title: Direct Selection: Shift-click deselects one anchor of a path selected whole
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
The plain click from #1254 (clicking an anchor of a selected shape with Direct Selection selects only that anchor) was already fixed by #1237, which was merged a minute before the issue was filed. I checked it on main through `Session::pointer` for a shape selected by command, with the Selection tool, inside a selected group, drawn with the Rectangle tool, and an ellipse. All of them end up with only the clicked anchor selected.

One case was still wrong: Shift-clicking an anchor of a path selected as a whole left only that anchor selected, instead of deselecting it and keeping the rest. The tool sends the right `select.anchors` toggle. The command started from an empty anchor set for a path stored as whole, though, so the toggle added the anchor instead of removing it. `add` mode had the same problem. Both now start from all the path's anchors when the path is selected whole, like `select.anchorsMany` already does. `set` mode is unchanged.

Tests: a command-level test for toggle and add on a whole path, and an engine test that selects a rectangle with the Selection tool, switches to Direct Selection and Shift-clicks a corner, expecting the other three anchors to stay selected. Both failed before the fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

Not verified: I didn't try it by hand in the desktop or web app.

title: perf: テクスチャ効果の距離判定を軽くする #1257
author: haranishi
body:
## What and why

Refs #1257

報告動画で使われている Round Corners + Craquelure の再描画で、画素ごとの近傍セル探索を軽くします。最大25セルの距離を二乗で比較し、丸め誤差や同距離の境界だけ従来の `hypot` 比較に戻します。同じ探索を使う Mosaic Tiles と Stained Glass にも効きます。効果設定と描画画素を維持します。

Windowsでのマウス追従は未確認です。このPRは再描画の計算量を減らす変更で、イシュー全体の解消には操作確認が残ります。進捗文書にも残件を記載し、スコア・工数は据え置きました。

## How it was tested

- macOSの `cargo xtask ci`: 全7工程成功、5,382件成功・0件失敗・5件ignored。
- 6,051通りの座標・点配置で、全25候補を列挙する独立した参照実装と最寄り2点が一致。負座標、セル境界、同距離、大きい座標、非有限値を含みます。既存の画素効果テストも46件成功。
- 自作のCMYK角丸矩形を190.07%・DPI 1.5で移動して描画。3効果それぞれの1800×1500画素のRGBA出力が、mainの出力と全バイト一致しました。
- 同じ開発ビルド・自作フィクスチャ・移動8フレームの中央値: Craquelure 152.45 → 110.38 ms、Mosaic Tiles 127.07 → 88.52 ms、Stained Glass 205.07 → 150.78 ms。高負荷の開発機での参考値です。Windowsの操作速度やアイドル時の性能を示す値ではありません。

- ネイティブアプリの `ui.pointer` でドラッグ: 図形の位置だけが変化し、効果設定と選択は維持。1操作のUndo/Redoで文書全体が元に戻ることと、描画画像を確認しました。`ui.screenshot` は `NoFrame` のため取得できず、OSの実マウス操作・表示フレームは未検証です。

title: fix: フォントのフルネームを正しい書体へ解決する #1258
author: haranishi
body:
## What and why

Refs #1258

インストール済みの書体をフルネームで指定すると、フォントが見つからず代替書体になる問題を直します。たとえばファミリー名 `Loop Script` とスタイル `Italic` は解決する一方、`Loop Script Italic` だけでは通常体の代替書体になっていました。

[OpenTypeの名前テーブル仕様](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/name#name-ids)にある name ID 4 を、その書体とスタイルの別名として登録します。読み込み済み・カタログ内の書体と、Missing Fontsのフォルダ検索で同じ照合を使います。日本語名も読み、名前を正規化する既存処理で空白とハイフンの違いを吸収します。実在するファミリー名を優先し、可変フォントのフルネームはデフォルトの書体を指すようにしました。

本イシューの拡張子なしフォントについては、現在のmainがOSから列挙されたファイルを拡張子で除外せず読み、既存回帰テストも成功しています。このPRはフルネーム照合の修正です。Windowsで実際に有効化されたフォントの読み込みは報告者の実機確認が残ります。関連資料のスコア・工数は据え置きました。

## How it was tested

- 自作の名前テーブルと既存OFLフォントで回帰テスト3件を追加。フルネームとPostScript名が異なる書体、ハイフン・大文字・日本語名、Missing Fontsの検索、実在するファミリー名の優先、可変フォントのデフォルトと別ウェイトを確認しました。修正前は2件失敗・1件成功、修正後は全件成功です。
- `cargo test -p vectorcraft-text`: 単体219件と統合1件が成功。フォント管理、文字組み、字形の既存テストも成功しました。
- 自作SVGを既存CLIで開くと、フルネーム指定の2行が `missing` と代替通常体になり、ファミリー＋スタイルとPostScript名の2行は正しい斜体になりました。修正後は同じCLIで4行とも `exact` で正しい斜体に解決し、Missing Fontsは0件。描画も確認しました。
- `cargo xtask ci`: macOSの全7工程成功、5,384件成功・0件失敗・4件ignored。
- ネイティブアプリでも同じSVGの4つの名前が正しい斜体に解決し、Missing Fontsは0件。情報照会と描画で文書が変わらず、`modified:null` で保存日時の更新を抑えた保存・再オープンでは文書全体と書体情報が一致しました。描画画像は確認済みです。`ui.screenshot` は `NoFrame` で取得できず、OSの実マウス操作・パネル表示は未検証です。

title: M2.x: Path Length panel (editable path length, object.setLength)
author: discocandyproductions
body:
Adds an editable total-length reading for the selection, something Illustrator's Document Info can only show read-only (Objects > Paths > "length = ..."), buried in a flyout menu, with no way to type a new value.

- object.setLength (crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs): sums the length of every NodeKind::Path in the selection's subtrees (a compound path's and a selected group's children included, via Node::walk) using the existing PathData::length() arc-length math, then uniformly scales the selection about its centre via the existing apply_transform/scaling machinery, so undo/redo, Transform Again, and the Scale Strokes & Effects / Scale Corners prefs all come for free. Session::selection_length() exposes the read for the panel. Rejects a non-positive length and a selection with no length to scale.
- New "Path Length" panel (crates/ui-egui/src/panels/path_length.rs): one editable field, disabled when nothing scalable is selected. Registered in ICON_PANELS/ICON_PANEL_GROUPS (state.rs) next to Transform, in the Window menu (menus.rs) and in panels/mod.rs. Uses the existing "ruler" icon; no new assets.
- Unit test (crates/engine/src/tests.rs): a 10x10 square (length 40) set to 80 doubles both sides; zero/negative lengths are rejected without changing the selection.

Verified: cargo check, cargo clippy -D warnings and cargo fmt --check on vectorcraft-engine and vectorcraft-ui-egui, plus the new test, all clean, both in the original source checkout and re-verified (check only) after rebasing onto this fork's current main.

title: perf: bounds cache, change sets and an R-tree for hover, marquee, snapping and drags (#1280)
author: arhammusheer
body:
Work in progress for #1280: hovering, hit testing, marquee, snapping and drags cost time in proportion to the whole document.

**Stacked on #1245.** This branch builds on it, because both change `Node` and the undo history. Until #1245 merges, this diff includes its commits; once it merges I'll rebase onto `main`. The commits for this PR start at "#1280".

## Baseline (50k paths, Apple M2 Pro, with #1245)

| | |
|---|---:|
| Hover over empty canvas | 16.8 ms |
| Hover over empty canvas, all selected | 66.7 ms |
| Hit test that misses | 8.2 ms |
| Marquee 400×300 | 8.2 ms |
| Drag the selection, per move | 67.6 ms |
| Nudge the selection | 71.9 ms |

## Scope

- Bounds cached per object, plus an allocation-free `PathData::bounds`.
- A change set from comparing old and new trees by `Arc` pointer, which is O(changed).
- An R-tree of object bounds, updated incrementally, used by hit testing, marquee, Direct Selection anchor picking and smart guides.
- Derived passes (Shaper, text wrap, inline symbols, selection checks) run only on changed subtrees.
- A hashed selection.
- Selection overlays culled to the view and drawn as one mesh, and the Layers panel's per-frame walks removed.

Results will be added here as commits land.

Closes #1280.

title: G2: add Artistic Film Grain live effect
author: Tevinhead
body:
## What and why

Adds **Effect → Artistic → Film Grain…**, the first Artistic raster filter. Dark fills and black now take visible monochrome grain, while lighter fills receive softer grain and white stays clean. Grain, Highlight Area and Intensity have bounded integer sliders with live preview, Cancel rollback, one-step undo and editing through Appearance. The effect works through the existing command, render, native save/open and SVG/PDF raster-baking paths.

The noise field uses two independently rotated, variance-normalised layers in document space, continuous transitions between footprint sampling modes, constant-size cell caches and an exact invisible-noise shortcut. All 11 shipped locales include the new labels; the shared control list feeds the translation inventory. Parity and roadmap counts advance to 29/57 Photoshop-style filters, with 28 still missing.

This is an original approximation of [publicly documented behavior](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop-elements/desktop/guided-edits-effects-and-filters/artistic-filters.html). No Adobe software was run or measured. The tonal curve, endpoint behavior, defaults and ranges are interpretations. A faint diagonal weave remains at high magnification; minification is approximate, saturated channels can clip, equal-sized duplicates share a pattern, and changing the bounds shifts it. Near white, headroom can flatten Intensity's grain control. Film Grain costs more per pixel than Texture Grain (Regular); these limits are documented.

title: Web: repair clipboard routing and preserve editing sessions
author: mmmbeer
body:

A browser gesture can arrive as a key and a clipboard payload in separate frames. This ports the existing *craft routing so one gesture causes one supported edit, publishes editable SVG text plus PNG, imports external text instead of stale artwork, preserves focused text controls and cancels asynchronous paste when the document or field selection changed.

Browser recovery checkpoints include new/unsaved documents, ordered tabs, active document, both history stacks, embedded image bytes, selections, tool/view state and preferences. Existing legacy browser recovery is retained for import while competing writes are disabled.

Validation: nine standalone storage tests passed for this app at the root URL; the common harness extracting the actual production clipboard routers/PNG decoder passed eight tests. title: Links: Find in Folder… looks for missing linked files in a folder and its subfolders
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What and why

When a document opens without its linked files, Linked File Not Found asks about each one. Replace with Apply to All
looks for the other files by name in the folder of the file picked, and the Links panel's Relink to Folder… looks in a
folder the user picks. Files kept in subfolders, or spread over several folders, had to be relinked one folder at a
time. The reference app's Search for Missing Links in this folder option relinks the other missing files it finds in the
folder of the file picked
([described by an Adobe community manager in May 2024](https://community.adobe.com/questions-652/i-can-t-see-button-search-for-missing-links-in-this-folder-option-on-adobe-illustator-810045?postid=2998796#post2998796)).

Find in Folder…, in Linked File Not Found and in the Links panel menu, looks in a folder the user picks and in its
subfolders for files with the names of the missing linked files, in any letter case. In the Links panel it looks for
the selected linked files when there are any. It uses the folder search of the Missing Fonts dialog (#792). Find Linked
Files lists each file it looks for with the files found for it. A file with the size and contents saved with the link
comes first (Same file). A file of the saved size comes next when the link saved no hash or the file is larger than
1 GB (Same size), and any other file of the name comes last. Within each group, a file named in the same letter case
comes first. Then each file's folder names are compared with the saved path's, from the innermost outward, up to the
first one that differs, and a file with more matching names comes before one with fewer.

- A file is chosen when it is the only file found, or the only Same file. The user can choose another file or Don't
  Relink. Relink relinks each file chosen, and each relink is one undo step.
